"""App factory and app-level plumbing: request id, CORS, error envelope, health."""

import logging
import uuid
from typing import Any

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.middleware.gzip import GZipMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from sqlalchemy.exc import DBAPIError
from starlette.datastructures import MutableHeaders
from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException
from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send

from app.core.audit import actor_user_id_ctx, request_id_ctx, request_ip_ctx
from app.core.config import Settings, get_settings
from app.core.docflow_router import router as docflow_router
from app.core.exceptions import AtlasError, translate_db_guard_error
from app.core.idempotency import REPLAYED_HEADER, IdempotencyReplay
from app.core.jobs_router import router as jobs_router
from app.core.rbac import current_permissions
from app.core.schemas import ErrorBody, ErrorEnvelope
from app.core.security_router import router as security_router
from app.core.tenancy import current_tenant_id
from app.modules.finance.router import router as finance_router
from app.modules.hr.router import router as hr_router
from app.modules.inventory.router import router as inventory_router
from app.modules.maintenance.router import router as maintenance_router
from app.modules.manufacturing.router import router as manufacturing_router
from app.modules.procurement.router import router as procurement_router
from app.modules.projects.router import router as projects_router
from app.modules.quality.router import router as quality_router
from app.modules.sales.router import router as sales_router

logger = logging.getLogger("atlas")

API_PREFIX = "/api/v1"

# request_id lives in the audit module (core/audit.py owns the request-context ContextVars);
# re-exported under the historical name so existing callers/tests keep one import.
request_id_var = request_id_ctx


def _client_ip(scope: Scope, trust_proxy: bool) -> str | None:
    """Audited client IP (D-010). Default: the raw transport peer (scope['client']). Only
    when ATLAS_TRUST_PROXY is on do we honor the LEFT-MOST X-Forwarded-For hop — otherwise a
    client could spoof its own audited IP just by sending the header."""
    if trust_proxy:
        for raw_name, raw_value in scope.get("headers", ()):
            if raw_name == b"x-forwarded-for":
                first_hop = raw_value.decode("latin-1").split(",")[0].strip()
                if first_hop:
                    return first_hop
    client = scope.get("client")
    return client[0] if client else None


class RequestIdMiddleware:
    """Pure-ASGI: one uuid4-hex request id per request, exposed via ContextVar,
    request.state and the X-Request-ID response header.

    It ALSO owns the D-007 tenancy-ContextVar reset, the D-009 current_permissions reset,
    and the D-010 audit-context (request_id, request_ip, actor_user_id) lifecycle:
    get_current_user sets the tenant/permissions/actor vars directly (no context manager),
    so this middleware captures reset tokens in a finally block — otherwise request A's
    context would leak into request B reusing the same worker/task. request_id and
    request_ip are seeded here at the edge; actor_user_id starts None (system/unauth) and is
    filled by get_current_user once the principal is known. All are reset on the way out, so
    the worker always restarts at the defaults."""

    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp, trust_proxy: bool) -> None:
        self.app = app
        self.trust_proxy = trust_proxy

    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        if scope["type"] != "http":
            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
            return
        request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
        scope.setdefault("state", {})["request_id"] = request_id
        token = request_id_var.set(request_id)
        ip_token = request_ip_ctx.set(_client_ip(scope, self.trust_proxy))
        actor_token = actor_user_id_ctx.set(None)
        tenant_token = current_tenant_id.set(None)
        permissions_token = current_permissions.set(frozenset())

        async def send_with_request_id(message: Message) -> None:
            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
                MutableHeaders(scope=message)["X-Request-ID"] = request_id
            await send(message)

        try:
            await self.app(scope, receive, send_with_request_id)
        finally:
            current_permissions.reset(permissions_token)
            current_tenant_id.reset(tenant_token)
            actor_user_id_ctx.reset(actor_token)
            request_ip_ctx.reset(ip_token)
            request_id_var.reset(token)


def _request_id(request: Request) -> str | None:
    # The ContextVar is already reset when the catch-all handler runs (Starlette's
    # ServerErrorMiddleware sits outside RequestIdMiddleware), hence the state fallback.
    return request_id_var.get() or getattr(request.state, "request_id", None)


def _error_response(
    request: Request,
    status_code: int,
    code: str,
    message: str,
    details: list[Any] | dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> JSONResponse:
    request_id = _request_id(request)
    envelope = ErrorEnvelope(
        error=ErrorBody(code=code, message=message, details=details, request_id=request_id)
    )
    # Set the header here too: 500 responses bypass RequestIdMiddleware's send wrapper.
    headers = {"X-Request-ID": request_id} if request_id else None
    return JSONResponse(status_code=status_code, content=envelope.model_dump(), headers=headers)


async def _handle_atlas_error(request: Request, exc: AtlasError) -> JSONResponse:
    return _error_response(request, exc.status_code, exc.code, exc.message, exc.details)


async def _handle_idempotency_replay(
    request: Request, exc: IdempotencyReplay
) -> JSONResponse:
    # D-013 replay short-circuit: a completed key with a matching body hash never runs the
    # handler. reserve() raised this carrying the stored status + body; we re-emit them verbatim
    # with the Idempotency-Replayed marker so the side effect cannot run twice. Registered BEFORE
    # the generic AtlasError handler (more specific subclass) so it wins dispatch.
    request_id = _request_id(request)
    headers = {REPLAYED_HEADER: "true"}
    if request_id:
        headers["X-Request-ID"] = request_id
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=exc.status_code, content=exc.response_body, headers=headers
    )


async def _handle_http_exception(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
    code = "common.not_found" if exc.status_code == 404 else "common.http_error"
    return _error_response(request, exc.status_code, code, str(exc.detail))


async def _handle_validation_error(
    request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError
) -> JSONResponse:
    details = [
        {
            "field": ".".join(str(part) for part in err.get("loc", ())),
            "message": err.get("msg", ""),
            "type": err.get("type", ""),
        }
        for err in exc.errors()
    ]
    return _error_response(
        request, 422, "common.validation_error", "Request validation failed", details
    )


async def _handle_db_guard_error(request: Request, exc: DBAPIError) -> JSONResponse:
    # D-014: a DB trigger that raised an ATLAS_* token surfaces through the same envelope
    # as service-level checks (e.g. ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY -> 409 audit.append_only). A
    # DBAPIError WITHOUT a known token is a genuine integrity/operational fault — log it and
    # return the opaque 500 like any unexpected error, never leaking raw DB text.
    translated = translate_db_guard_error(exc)
    if translated is not None:
        return _error_response(
            request, translated.status_code, translated.code, translated.message
        )
    logger.exception("Database error (request_id=%s)", _request_id(request), exc_info=exc)
    return _error_response(request, 500, "common.internal_error", "Internal server error")


async def _handle_unexpected_error(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
    # Log with request id; never leak the traceback into the response body.
    logger.exception("Unhandled error (request_id=%s)", _request_id(request), exc_info=exc)
    return _error_response(request, 500, "common.internal_error", "Internal server error")


def create_app(settings: Settings | None = None) -> FastAPI:
    settings = settings or get_settings()
    logging.basicConfig(level=settings.log_level.upper())

    app = FastAPI(
        title="Atlas ERP",
        version="0.1.0",
        openapi_url=f"{API_PREFIX}/openapi.json",
        docs_url=f"{API_PREFIX}/docs",
        redoc_url=None,
    )

    app.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=settings.cors_origins,
        allow_credentials=True,
        allow_methods=["*"],
        allow_headers=["*"],
    )
    # Response compression (PERFORMANCE §3): bodies >= 500 bytes are gzipped when the client
    # sends Accept-Encoding: gzip; tiny responses pass through uncompressed. Added between
    # CORS and RequestIdMiddleware, so the request id header is stamped outside compression.
    app.add_middleware(GZipMiddleware, minimum_size=500)
    # Added last == outermost user middleware: the request id exists for everything
    # below it, including CORS rejections.
    app.add_middleware(RequestIdMiddleware, trust_proxy=settings.trust_proxy)

    # IdempotencyReplay is an AtlasError subclass; register it FIRST so Starlette dispatches a
    # replay to its verbatim-response handler before the generic envelope handler (D-013).
    app.add_exception_handler(IdempotencyReplay, _handle_idempotency_replay)
    app.add_exception_handler(AtlasError, _handle_atlas_error)
    app.add_exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException, _handle_http_exception)
    app.add_exception_handler(RequestValidationError, _handle_validation_error)
    # DBAPIError is more specific than Exception, so Starlette dispatches DB-guard tokens
    # (D-014) here before falling through to the catch-all 500 below.
    app.add_exception_handler(DBAPIError, _handle_db_guard_error)
    app.add_exception_handler(Exception, _handle_unexpected_error)

    @app.get(f"{API_PREFIX}/health")
    async def health() -> dict[str, str]:
        return {"status": "ok", "env": settings.env}

    # Core platform auth endpoints (D-008): login/refresh/logout/me at /api/v1/auth.
    app.include_router(security_router)
    # Core platform document-flow read endpoint (D-012): GET /api/v1/documents/{id}/chain.
    app.include_router(docflow_router)
    # Core platform background-job polling (PLAN 4P.5/D-032): GET /api/v1/jobs[/{id}].
    app.include_router(jobs_router)
    # Finance module (PLAN 4): chart of accounts + fiscal years/periods at /api/v1/finance.
    # First business module mounted; the fixed import order here is also the D-011 handler
    # registration order (finance, then inventory, ...) once modules publish/subscribe events.
    app.include_router(finance_router)
    # Inventory module (PLAN 5): item masters at /api/v1/inventory. Mounted after finance, the
    # D-011 handler-registration order; inventory reads finance/queries downward (STRUCTURE §5).
    app.include_router(inventory_router)
    # Procurement module (PLAN 6): vendor master at /api/v1/procurement. Mounted after inventory,
    # the D-011 handler-registration order; procurement OWNS the vendor entity and reads
    # finance/queries + inventory/queries downward (STRUCTURE §5 / D-029).
    app.include_router(procurement_router)
    # Sales module (PLAN 7): customer master + condition-style pricing at /api/v1/sales. Mounted
    # after procurement, the D-011 handler-registration order; sales OWNS the customer entity and
    # reads finance/queries + inventory/queries downward (STRUCTURE §5 / D-029). 7.1 publishes no
    # cross-module events (masters + pricing drive no effects; orders in 7.2 will).
    app.include_router(sales_router)
    # Manufacturing module (PLAN 8): PP master data (work centres, multi-level versioned BOMs,
    # routings) at /api/v1/manufacturing. Mounted after sales, the D-011 handler-registration
    # order; manufacturing reads finance/queries + inventory/queries downward (STRUCTURE §5 /
    # D-029). 8.1 publishes no cross-module events (masters drive no effects; production orders in
    # 8.2 will).
    app.include_router(manufacturing_router)
    # Quality module (PLAN 9): inspection lots at /api/v1/quality. Mounted after manufacturing, the
    # D-011 handler-registration order; quality SUBSCRIBES to procurement's GoodsReceiptPosted to
    # create inspection lots and reads inventory/queries downward (STRUCTURE §5 / D-029 / D-050). A
    # reject disposition publishes InspectionDispositioned → inventory moves the rejected stock.
    app.include_router(quality_router)
    # Maintenance module (PLAN 9.2): equipment + corrective/preventive orders + interval plans at
    # /api/v1/maintenance. Mounted after quality, the D-011 module import order; maintenance reads
    # finance/queries downward for an equipment's optional cost centre (STRUCTURE §5 / D-029 /
    # D-051). It publishes/subscribes to NO cross-module event in v1 — a completed order records its
    # cost on the order row (record-only, no GL posting, D-051).
    app.include_router(maintenance_router)
    # HR module (PLAN 10.1): employees (masked compensation/PII), departments, positions, org chart
    # at /api/v1/hr. Mounted after maintenance, the D-011 module import order; hr reads
    # finance/queries downward for a department's optional cost centre and probes core_users for an
    # employee's optional login (STRUCTURE §5 / D-029 / D-052). It is the FIRST real use of the
    # D-009
    # field-masking serializer (compensation/PII behind hr.employee.read_compensation). PLAN 10.4
    # adds payroll: HR PUBLISHES its first cross-module event (PayrollPosted) and finance posts the
    # consolidated payroll journal through the bus (D-055).
    app.include_router(hr_router)
    # Projects module (PLAN 11.1): projects + a WBS-element tree as COSTING OBJECTS + the project
    # cost report at /api/v1/projects. Mounted after hr, the D-011 module import order; projects is
    # the TOP of the dependency order — it reads finance/queries (cost-centre existence +
    # costs_by_project_dimension, the journal projection of actuals by the opaque WBS dimension),
    # hr/queries (approved hours by WBS), and sales/queries (customer existence) DOWNWARD (STRUCTURE
    # §5 / D-029 / D-056). It publishes/subscribes to NO cross-module event — projects is masters +
    # a READ report; "posting time/purchases to a WBS" means a journal line / timesheet tags the WBS
    # id as its opaque project dimension, projects posts nothing itself (D-056).
    app.include_router(projects_router)

    # Cross-module event handlers (D-011): registered here, at the app factory, so registration
    # order
    # is the deterministic module import order. Importing the module runs its ``@on`` subscriptions.
    # finance/handlers posts the COGS/inventory journal for an inventory ``stock.valued`` event in
    # the
    # SAME transaction as the move (PLAN 5.3, D-020) — the first real cross-module handler.
    register_event_handlers()

    return app


def register_event_handlers() -> None:
    """Register the cross-module domain-event handlers (D-011), in the deterministic module order.

    Called from ``create_app`` (the registration seam) and available to seed/CLI flows that build
    the
    bus without the HTTP app. IDEMPOTENT and re-runnable: each handler is (re)subscribed only if not
    already present for its key, so building several apps in one process — or re-registering after
    the
    test harness's ``clear_subscriptions`` reset (D-025) — yields exactly one subscription per
    handler, never a duplicate that would double-post."""
    from app.core.events import handlers_for, subscribe
    from app.modules.finance.handlers import (
        create_bill_for_match,
        create_credit_note_for_return,
        create_invoice_for_billing,
        create_payroll_journal,
        post_production_variance,
        post_stock_valuation_journal,
    )
    from app.modules.hr.events import PayrollPosted
    from app.modules.inventory.events import StockValued
    from app.modules.inventory.handlers import (
        disposition_rejected_stock,
        issue_delivery_moves,
        issue_production_components,
        receive_finished_order_move,
        receive_goods_receipt_moves,
        receive_return_moves,
    )
    from app.modules.manufacturing.events import (
        ComponentsIssued,
        OrderFinished,
        PlannedBuyConverted,
    )
    from app.modules.procurement.events import GoodsReceiptPosted, InvoiceMatched
    from app.modules.procurement.handlers import create_requisition_for_planned_buy
    from app.modules.quality.events import InspectionDispositioned
    from app.modules.quality.handlers import create_inspection_lots_for_receipt
    from app.modules.sales.events import (
        BillingInvoiced,
        DeliveryShipped,
        ReturnCredited,
        ReturnReceived,
    )

    if post_stock_valuation_journal not in handlers_for(StockValued.key):
        subscribe(StockValued.key, post_stock_valuation_journal)
    # Procurement goods-receipt → inventory stock-move bridge (PLAN 6.3, D-041): inventory's
    # handler creates the RECEIPT moves (Cr GR-IR) when a GR posts, which in turn publish
    # StockValued for the finance handler above — a two-hop same-transaction chain
    # (procurement → inventory → finance).
    if receive_goods_receipt_moves not in handlers_for(GoodsReceiptPosted.key):
        subscribe(GoodsReceiptPosted.key, receive_goods_receipt_moves)
    # Sales delivery → inventory stock-move bridge (PLAN 7.3, D-045): the OUTBOUND twin of the GR
    # bridge — inventory's handler creates the ISSUE moves (Dr COGS / Cr Inventory, COGS the default
    # issue offset — no override) when a delivery posts, which in turn publish StockValued for the
    # finance handler above — the same two-hop same-transaction chain (sales → inventory → finance).
    if issue_delivery_moves not in handlers_for(DeliveryShipped.key):
        subscribe(DeliveryShipped.key, issue_delivery_moves)
    # Procurement invoice-match → finance AP-bill bridge (PLAN 6.4, D-042): finance's handler
    # creates + posts the matched vendor bill (Dr GR/IR + PPV / Cr AP) when a match posts, clearing
    # the GR/IR account the goods receipt credited — closing the procure-to-pay loop. Procurement
    # publishes; finance handles its own bill posting (STRUCTURE §5).
    if create_bill_for_match not in handlers_for(InvoiceMatched.key):
        subscribe(InvoiceMatched.key, create_bill_for_match)
    # Sales billing → finance AR-invoice bridge (PLAN 7.4, D-046): the MIRROR of the invoice-match →
    # AP-bill bridge, sign-flipped — finance's handler creates + posts the AR customer invoice (Dr
    # AR
    # control / Cr revenue + tax) when a billing posts. Sales publishes; finance handles its own
    # invoice posting (STRUCTURE §5).
    if create_invoice_for_billing not in handlers_for(BillingInvoiced.key):
        subscribe(BillingInvoiced.key, create_invoice_for_billing)
    # Sales return → inventory RECEIPT bridge (PLAN 7.4, D-046): inventory's handler receives the
    # goods back (Dr Inventory / Cr COGS via the COGS-offset override — reversing the delivery's
    # issue) when a return posts, which publishes StockValued for the finance COGS handler above.
    if receive_return_moves not in handlers_for(ReturnReceived.key):
        subscribe(ReturnReceived.key, receive_return_moves)
    # Sales return → finance AR-credit-note bridge (PLAN 7.4, D-046): finance's handler creates +
    # posts the AR credit note (Dr revenue / Cr AR + reverse tax — reversing the billing) when a
    # return posts. The second leg of an atomic return post (the first is the stock receipt above).
    if create_credit_note_for_return not in handlers_for(ReturnCredited.key):
        subscribe(ReturnCredited.key, create_credit_note_for_return)
    # Manufacturing production-order → inventory stock-move bridges (PLAN 8.2, D-048), the
    # manufacturing↔inventory↔finance seam. A component ISSUE posts Dr WIP / Cr Inventory (the
    # valuation-offset OVERRIDE to the WIP account — the 6.3 GR/IR-override pattern applied to an
    # ISSUE) and a finished RECEIPT posts Dr Inventory / Cr WIP, both via inventory's handlers
    # creating the moves which in turn publish StockValued for the finance handler above — the same
    # two-hop same-transaction chain (manufacturing → inventory → finance). WIP nets to zero per
    # fully-issued + finished order; the variance flush is posted by manufacturing's finish flow.
    if issue_production_components not in handlers_for(ComponentsIssued.key):
        subscribe(ComponentsIssued.key, issue_production_components)
    # OrderFinished has TWO same-transaction subscribers: inventory's handler creates the finished
    # RECEIPT move (Dr Inventory / Cr WIP) and finance's handler posts the residual WIP variance (so
    # WIP nets to zero). Both drain in the finish's uow; either failure rolls the whole finish back.
    if receive_finished_order_move not in handlers_for(OrderFinished.key):
        subscribe(OrderFinished.key, receive_finished_order_move)
    if post_production_variance not in handlers_for(OrderFinished.key):
        subscribe(OrderFinished.key, post_production_variance)
    # Manufacturing planned-BUY → procurement DRAFT-requisition bridge (PLAN 8.3, D-049): a planned
    # BUY order's conversion publishes PlannedBuyConverted and procurement's handler creates the
    # requisition in the SAME transaction, linking the MRP run document → 'planned_to' → requisition
    # (the §5-clean planned-BUY → requisition mechanism — manufacturing never imports procurement
    # service, the billing → AR-invoice precedent).
    if create_requisition_for_planned_buy not in handlers_for(PlannedBuyConverted.key):
        subscribe(PlannedBuyConverted.key, create_requisition_for_planned_buy)
    # GoodsReceiptPosted has TWO same-transaction subscribers (PLAN 9.1, D-050): inventory's
    # receive_goods_receipt_moves (registered above) creates the RECEIPT moves, then quality's
    # create_inspection_lots_for_receipt creates an OPEN inspection lot per requires_inspection
    # line.
    # Quality is subscribed AFTER inventory (registration order = dispatch order, D-011) so the
    # lot/serial master instance the receipt creates already exists when quality resolves the GR
    # line's code to a traceability id.
    if create_inspection_lots_for_receipt not in handlers_for(GoodsReceiptPosted.key):
        subscribe(GoodsReceiptPosted.key, create_inspection_lots_for_receipt)
    # Quality reject-disposition → inventory stock-move bridge (PLAN 9.1, D-050): a REJECT usage
    # decision publishes InspectionDispositioned and inventory's handler moves the rejected stock
    # (SCRAP = an ADJUSTMENT-out write-off → Dr inventory-adjustment / Cr Inventory; BLOCK = a
    # value-neutral TRANSFER to the blocked bin) in the SAME transaction. Quality publishes;
    # inventory handles its own move (STRUCTURE §5). An ACCEPT publishes nothing — accepted stock is
    # already received and usable.
    if disposition_rejected_stock not in handlers_for(InspectionDispositioned.key):
        subscribe(InspectionDispositioned.key, disposition_rejected_stock)
    # HR payroll → finance consolidated-journal bridge (PLAN 10.4, D-055), HR's FIRST cross-module
    # event: a payroll-run post publishes PayrollPosted and finance's create_payroll_journal posts
    # the consolidated journal (Dr salary-expense by cost centre / Cr payroll-tax-payable / Cr
    # wages-payable — balanced because gross = tax + net) in the SAME transaction, linking the run
    # document → 'posts' → journal. HR publishes; finance handles its own journal posting (HR never
    # imports finance/service — STRUCTURE §5), the match → AP-bill / billing → AR-invoice precedent.
    if create_payroll_journal not in handlers_for(PayrollPosted.key):
        subscribe(PayrollPosted.key, create_payroll_journal)


app = create_app()

5	lines (a positive net = a debit, a negative net = a credit), carrying the item dimension. Used by
6	the inventory-COGS and production-variance handlers, which both build their entries from a signed
7	posting list.

11	
12	import uuid
13	from decimal import Decimal
14	
15	from app.modules.finance.schemas import JournalLineCreate
16	
17	# A signed posting (account_id, amount): positive => debit, negative => credit; the line builder
18	# drops zeros and splits into one-sided debit/credit lines.
19	_SignedPosting = tuple[uuid.UUID, Decimal]
20	
21	
22	def _lines_from_postings(
23	    postings: list[_SignedPosting], item_id: uuid.UUID
24	) -> list[JournalLineCreate]:
25	    """Collapse signed postings per account, drop zeros, and emit one-sided journal lines (D-017):
26	    a positive net is a debit, a negative net a credit. The item dimension rides every line so the
27	    COGS entry is attributable to the item (D-017 dimensions)."""
28	    net: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = {}
29	    for account_id, signed in postings:
30	        net[account_id] = net.get(account_id, Decimal(0)) + signed
31	    lines: list[JournalLineCreate] = []
32	    for account_id, value in net.items():
33	        if value == 0:
34	            continue
35	        if value > 0:
36	            lines.append(
37	                JournalLineCreate(
38	                    account_id=account_id,
39	                    transaction_debit_amount=value,
40	                    item_id=item_id,
41	                )
42	            )
43	        else:
44	            lines.append(
45	                JournalLineCreate(
46	                    account_id=account_id,
47	                    transaction_credit_amount=-value,
48	                    item_id=item_id,
49	                )
50	            )

29	"""

31	from enum import StrEnum

33	from app.core.rbac import register_permissions

36	# given the service cycle guard) cannot spin forever — the department/equipment-hierarchy precedent
37	# (D-052). A practical project breakdown is a handful of levels deep; 64 is generous headroom.
38	MAX_WBS_DEPTH = 64

41	class ProjectStatus(StrEnum):
42	    """Lifecycle of a PROJECT (PLAN 11.1, D-056). The service owns every transition (CLAUDE.md
43	    rule 7); v1 keeps the lifecycle informational — it does NOT gate posting (finance/HR tag a WBS
44	    id opaquely and never consult project status, D-029).
45	
46	    - **PLANNING** — being set up (WBS being authored). The default at creation.
47	    - **ACTIVE** — in execution; the project the cost report is most often run against.
48	    - **CLOSED** — completed; kept for historical cost reporting. Terminal.
49	    - **CANCELLED** — abandoned. Terminal.
50	    """

52	    PLANNING = "PLANNING"
53	    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
54	    CLOSED = "CLOSED"
55	    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"

60	    CLOSED, an informational flag on the masters.
61	
62	    - **OPEN** — the costing object accepts further postings (the default at creation).
63	    - **CLOSED** — closed to FURTHER postings. v1 records this as a flag ONLY: finance/HR tag the
64	      WBS id opaquely and do NOT consult WBS status before posting (D-029 keeps finance at the
65	      bottom — it would need to import projects to check, which is forbidden). The closed flag is
66	      therefore advisory in v1; a posting-time block would require a projects-owned posting gate,
67	      a documented later (D-056). It still surfaces on the cost report so a reader sees which

77	# read key so a controller can be granted the report without WBS-edit rights (segregation of duties:
78	# reading project cost is distinct from authoring the structure).

95	        PROJECTS_WBS_MANAGE: "Create and edit WBS elements",

2	the ``Project`` master and its ``WbsElement`` tree.
3	
4	TWO tables, one concern (PS v1 cost collection) — well under the 400-line cap, so a single
5	models.py (the maintenance/quality precedent; split into a models/ package only at the cap).
6	
7	- ``Project`` and ``WbsElement`` are both MASTERS keyed by a USER-SUPPLIED ``code`` (no gapless
8	  document number — the work-centre / equipment precedent). Neither mixes in DocumentMixin: a
9	  project/WBS is reference data a posting TAGS, not a posted docflow document (D-056). The
10	  ``Project`` code is UNIQUE per tenant; the ``WbsElement`` code is UNIQUE per (tenant, project) —
11	  it only has to be unique within its project (the account-group-within-chart precedent).
12	
13	- A ``WbsElement``'s ``id`` IS THE COSTING OBJECT (D-056): it is the opaque ``project_id`` dimension
14	  a finance journal line / HR time entry tags when work / purchases are "posted to a WBS". The cost
15	  report projects journal lines + timesheet hours by that id.

18	(nullable, validated via ``sales/queries.customer_exists`` when set — never a cross-module FK).
19	``Project.cost_center_id`` is an OPAQUE finance cost-centre id (nullable, validated via
20	``finance/queries.cost_center_exists`` when set). The ``project_id`` / ``parent_id`` links are
21	INTRA-module composite tenant FKs (the WBS tree + its owning project).

23	Money columns use the D-015 ``MoneyType`` (scale-6, exact on both engines); a plain ``sa.Numeric``
24	would round-trip through float on SQLite and lose precision, so it is never used for a stored amount
25	here. ``budget_amount`` is a SIMPLE budget figure feeding the cost report's variance — NOT a
26	budget-control mechanism (no posting-time funds check in v1, D-056).
27	"""

54	    ``status`` runs the ``ProjectStatus`` lifecycle (informational in v1 — it does NOT gate posting,
55	    D-029). ``customer_id`` is an OPAQUE sales customer id (nullable, validated via sales/queries
56	    when set — a project may be for a customer). ``cost_center_id`` is an OPAQUE finance cost-centre
57	    id (nullable, validated via finance/queries when set — for cost attribution). ``start_date`` /

98	class WbsElement(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
99	    """A WBS ELEMENT (D-056): a node in a project's work-breakdown tree and THE COSTING OBJECT.
100	
101	    ``project_id`` is the INTRA-module composite tenant FK to the owning ``ps_projects`` row.
102	    ``code`` is USER-SUPPLIED and unique per (tenant, PROJECT) — it only has to be unique within its
103	    project (the account-group-within-chart precedent). ``parent_id`` (nullable self composite
104	    tenant FK) builds the WBS TREE; the service cycle-guards it. ``status`` runs the ``WbsStatus``
105	    lifecycle (OPEN/CLOSED — advisory in v1, D-056). ``is_billable`` flags billable work (default
106	    false). ``budget_amount`` is the per-WBS budget feeding the cost report's per-element variance
107	    (MoneyType, nullable — NOT budget control).

110	    (``fin_journal_lines.project_id``) and a HR time entry (``hr_time_entries.project_id``) tag when
111	    work / purchases are posted to this WBS (D-056). Audited (D-010): the costing-object master.

114	    __tablename__ = "ps_wbs_elements"

133	        sa.Index(
134	            "ix_ps_wbs_elements_tenant_id_project_id_status",
135	            "tenant_id",
136	            "project_id",
137	            "status",
138	        ),
139	        sa.Index("ix_ps_wbs_elements_tenant_id_parent_id", "tenant_id", "parent_id"),
140	    )
141	
142	    project_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
143	    code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=False)
144	    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
145	    # Self composite tenant FK (nullable — a top-level WBS has no parent): the WBS tree.
146	    parent_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
147	    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
148	        sa.String(20),
149	        nullable=False,
150	        default=WbsStatus.OPEN.value,
151	        server_default="OPEN",
152	    )
153	    is_billable: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
154	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=False, server_default=sa.false()
155	    )
156	    budget_amount: Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(MoneyType(), nullable=True)

1	"""Project business logic (PLAN 11.1, D-056): CRUD + customer / cost-centre validation.
2	
3	The service layer owns every rule (CLAUDE.md rule 7); the router stays thin. The optional
4	``customer_id`` is an OPAQUE sales customer id (D-029): validated to exist via
5	``sales/queries.customer_exists`` (the sanctioned cross-module read, STRUCTURE §5) — never a
6	cross-module FK. The optional ``cost_center_id`` is an OPAQUE finance cost-centre id validated via
7	``finance/queries.cost_center_exists``. ``from __future__ import annotations`` keeps
8	``Page[Project]`` (the ORM model) a string at import; the router re-validates page items.
9	"""
10	
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import uuid
14	
15	from sqlalchemy import select
16	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
17	
18	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationFailedError
19	from app.core.pagination import DEFAULT_LIMIT, OrderKey, SortDirection, filter_fingerprint, paginate
20	from app.core.schemas import Page
21	from app.modules.finance import queries as finance_queries
22	from app.modules.projects.models import Project
23	from app.modules.projects.schemas import ProjectCreate, ProjectFilter, ProjectUpdate
24	from app.modules.sales import queries as sales_queries
25	
26	
27	async def _validate_customer(
28	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID | None
29	) -> None:
30	    """A supplied customer id must exist in sales (D-029): validated via the sales queries contract,
31	    never a cross-module FK. None is skipped (the customer is optional)."""
32	    if customer_id is None:
33	        return
34	    if not await sales_queries.customer_exists(session, tenant_id, customer_id):
35	        raise ValidationFailedError(
36	            message="Referenced customer does not exist",
37	            code="projects.customer_not_found",
38	            details={"customer_id": str(customer_id)},
39	        )
40	
41	
42	async def _validate_cost_center(
43	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, cost_center_id: uuid.UUID | None
44	) -> None:
45	    """A supplied cost-centre id must exist in finance (D-029): validated via the finance queries
46	    contract, never a cross-module FK. None is skipped (the cost centre is optional)."""
47	    if cost_center_id is None:
48	        return
49	    if not await finance_queries.cost_center_exists(session, tenant_id, cost_center_id):
50	        raise ValidationFailedError(
51	            message="Referenced cost centre does not exist",
52	            code="projects.cost_center_not_found",
53	            details={"cost_center_id": str(cost_center_id)},
54	        )
55	
56	
57	async def get_project(
58	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, project_id: uuid.UUID
59	) -> Project:
60	    project = await session.get(Project, project_id)
61	    if project is None or project.tenant_id != tenant_id:
62	        raise NotFoundError(message="Project not found", code="projects.project_not_found")
63	    return project
64	
65	
66	async def create_project(
67	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: ProjectCreate
68	) -> Project:
69	    """Create a project. Rejects a duplicate code (the DB UNIQUE is the backstop); validates the
70	    customer + cost centre exist when set."""
71	    existing = (
72	        await session.execute(
73	            select(Project.id).where(
74	                Project.tenant_id == tenant_id, Project.code == payload.code
75	            )
76	        )
77	    ).first()
78	    if existing is not None:
79	        raise ConflictError(
80	            message=f"Project with code {payload.code} already exists",
81	            code="projects.project_code_conflict",
82	            details={"code": payload.code},
83	        )
84	    await _validate_customer(session, tenant_id, payload.customer_id)
85	    await _validate_cost_center(session, tenant_id, payload.cost_center_id)
86	    project = Project(
87	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
88	        code=payload.code,
89	        name=payload.name,
90	        description=payload.description,
91	        # ApiModel sets use_enum_values=True, so payload enum fields are already their string value.
92	        status=payload.status,
93	        customer_id=payload.customer_id,
94	        cost_center_id=payload.cost_center_id,
95	        start_date=payload.start_date,
96	        end_date=payload.end_date,
97	        budget_amount=payload.budget_amount,
98	        is_active=payload.is_active,
99	    )
100	    session.add(project)
101	    await session.flush()
102	    return project
103	
104	
105	async def update_project(
106	    session: AsyncSession,
107	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
108	    project_id: uuid.UUID,
109	    payload: ProjectUpdate,
110	) -> Project:
111	    """Partial update (D-010: mutate the loaded object so the audit diff is captured). ``code`` is
112	    immutable and absent from the schema; a changed customer / cost centre is re-validated."""
113	    project = await get_project(session, tenant_id, project_id)
114	    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
115	    if "customer_id" in data:
116	        await _validate_customer(session, tenant_id, data["customer_id"])
117	    if "cost_center_id" in data:
118	        await _validate_cost_center(session, tenant_id, data["cost_center_id"])
119	    for field, value in data.items():
120	        setattr(project, field, value)
121	    await session.flush()
122	    return project
123	
124	
125	async def list_projects(
126	    session: AsyncSession,
127	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
128	    *,
129	    filters: ProjectFilter,
130	    cursor: str | None = None,
131	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
132	) -> Page[Project]:
133	    """Keyset-paginated projects ordered by code (D-014). The status filter narrows the set
134	    (index-served by (tenant, status)) and folds into the cursor fingerprint so a cursor cannot
135	    bleed across views."""
136	    stmt = select(Project).where(Project.tenant_id == tenant_id)

139	    fingerprint = filter_fingerprint(filters.status)
140	    return await paginate(
141	        session,
142	        stmt,
143	        order_by=[OrderKey(Project.code, SortDirection.ASC)],
144	        pk=Project.id,
145	        cursor=cursor,
146	        limit=limit,
147	        filters=fingerprint,
148	    )

5	stable. The service and router use these reads too. Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id``

7	tenant-scoped reads.

1	"""Projects HTTP layer (thin): parse -> call service -> return schema (PLAN 11.1).
2	
3	REST under ``/api/v1/projects``: projects (CRUD + filtered list + the cost report) here, with the
4	WBS-element surface (``wbs_router``, nested under a project) mounted as a sibling sub-router at the
5	foot of this file so the whole module is ONE surface at ``/api/v1/projects`` — the maintenance
6	order_router / plan_router include precedent (no second mount in main.py). Every route is guarded by
7	a projects permission key (D-009); writes commit through ``run_in_uow`` (D-011) so audit rows ride
8	the same transaction. The project list is reference data, so it carries a conditional-GET ETag
9	(PERFORMANCE §3 / D-035). The cost report is a bounded journal projection (PERFORMANCE §6 / D-056) —
10	guarded by the dedicated ``projects.report.read`` key.
11	"""
12	
13	import uuid
14	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
15	from datetime import date
16	
17	from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request, Response
18	
19	from app.core.conditional import collection_etag, conditional_response, request_fingerprint
20	from app.core.deps import CurrentUserDep, SessionDep
21	from app.core.events import run_in_uow
22	from app.core.pagination import CursorParams, cursor_params, map_page
23	from app.core.rbac import require_permission
24	from app.core.schemas import Page
25	from app.modules.projects import service
26	from app.modules.projects.constants import (
27	    PROJECTS_PROJECT_MANAGE,
28	    PROJECTS_PROJECT_READ,
29	    PROJECTS_REPORT_READ,
30	    ProjectStatus,
31	)
32	from app.modules.projects.models import Project
33	from app.modules.projects.schemas import (
34	    ProjectCostReport,
35	    ProjectCreate,
36	    ProjectFilter,
37	    ProjectRead,
38	    ProjectUpdate,
39	)
40	from app.modules.projects.wbs_router import wbs_router
41	
42	router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1/projects", tags=["projects"])
43	_CursorParamsDep = Depends(cursor_params)
44	
45	
46	async def _commit[T](session: SessionDep, work: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]) -> T:
47	    """Run a service call inside the D-011 uow, refreshing the ORM result in the async context so a
48	    sync ``model_validate`` never trips MissingGreenlet (the maintenance _commit twin)."""
49	    holder: list[T] = []
50	
51	    async def _work() -> None:
52	        result = await work()
53	        await session.refresh(result)
54	        holder.append(result)
55	
56	    await run_in_uow(session, _work)
57	    return holder[0]
58	
59	
60	@router.get(
61	    "",
62	    response_model=Page[ProjectRead],
63	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(PROJECTS_PROJECT_READ))],
64	)
65	async def list_projects(
66	    request: Request,
67	    response: Response,
68	    current: CurrentUserDep,
69	    session: SessionDep,
70	    params: CursorParams = _CursorParamsDep,
71	    status: ProjectStatus | None = None,
72	) -> Page[ProjectRead] | Response:
73	    """Conditional-GET supported (D-035): collection ETag over the project reference list; the
74	    status filter folds into the request fingerprint so a filtered 304 is correct."""
75	    filters = ProjectFilter(status=status)
76	    fingerprint = request_fingerprint(params.cursor, params.limit, status)
77	    etag = await collection_etag(session, Project, request_fingerprint=fingerprint)
78	
79	    async def builder() -> Page[ProjectRead]:
80	        page = await service.list_projects(
81	            session,
82	            current.tenant_id,
83	            filters=filters,
84	            cursor=params.cursor,
85	            limit=params.limit,
86	        )
87	        return map_page(page, ProjectRead)
88	
89	    return await conditional_response(request, response, etag, builder)
90	
91	
92	@router.post(
93	    "",
94	    response_model=ProjectRead,
95	    status_code=201,
96	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(PROJECTS_PROJECT_MANAGE))],
97	)
98	async def create_project(
99	    payload: ProjectCreate, current: CurrentUserDep, session: SessionDep
100	) -> ProjectRead:
101	    project = await _commit(
102	        session, lambda: service.create_project(session, current.tenant_id, payload)
103	    )
104	    return ProjectRead.model_validate(project)
105	
106	
107	@router.get(
108	    "/{project_id}",
109	    response_model=ProjectRead,
110	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(PROJECTS_PROJECT_READ))],
111	)
112	async def get_project(
113	    project_id: uuid.UUID, current: CurrentUserDep, session: SessionDep
114	) -> ProjectRead:
115	    project = await service.get_project(session, current.tenant_id, project_id)
116	    return ProjectRead.model_validate(project)
117	
118	
119	@router.patch(
120	    "/{project_id}",
121	    response_model=ProjectRead,
122	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(PROJECTS_PROJECT_MANAGE))],
123	)
124	async def update_project(
125	    project_id: uuid.UUID,
126	    payload: ProjectUpdate,
127	    current: CurrentUserDep,
128	    session: SessionDep,
129	) -> ProjectRead:
130	    project = await _commit(
131	        session,
132	        lambda: service.update_project(session, current.tenant_id, project_id, payload),
133	    )
134	    return ProjectRead.model_validate(project)
135	
136	
137	@router.get(
138	    "/{project_id}/cost-report",
139	    response_model=ProjectCostReport,
140	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(PROJECTS_REPORT_READ))],
141	)
142	async def get_cost_report(
143	    project_id: uuid.UUID,
144	    current: CurrentUserDep,
145	    session: SessionDep,
146	    as_of: date | None = None,
147	) -> ProjectCostReport:
148	    """The project cost report (D-056): per-WBS actuals (finance journal projection) + approved
149	    hours (hr) + budget variance, rolled up to the project. A bounded projection (PERFORMANCE §6) —
150	    read via finance/hr queries, not their services. ``as_of`` bounds the actuals cumulatively."""
151	    return await service.project_cost_report(
152	        session, current.tenant_id, project_id, as_of=as_of
153	    )
154	
155	
156	# The WBS-element surface (CRUD nested under a project + the tree) is a sibling sub-router mounted
157	# here, so the whole module is ONE surface at /api/v1/projects.
158	router.include_router(wbs_router)

12	# cannot drop unnamed constraints (D-022).
13	NAMING_CONVENTION = {
14	    "ix": "ix_%(column_0_label)s",
15	    "uq": "uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s",
16	    "ck": "ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s",
17	    "fk": "fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s",
18	    "pk": "pk_%(table_name)s",
19	}

21	# Portable JSON: JSONB on Postgres, plain JSON elsewhere. Type variance lives in
22	# the models so migrations import it from here and stay dialect-clean (D-022).
23	JSON_VARIANT = sa.JSON().with_variant(postgresql.JSONB(), "postgresql")
24	
25	
26	class Base(DeclarativeBase):
27	    metadata = sa.MetaData(naming_convention=NAMING_CONVENTION)
28	
29	
30	class UuidPKMixin:
31	    """uuid4 primary key, client-generated so ids are portable across both engines."""
32	
33	    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)

35	
36	class TenantMixin:
37	    """Row-level tenancy marker (D-007). Filtering and stamping are enforced by the
38	    core/tenancy.py session listeners; query authors never touch tenant_id."""
39	
40	    @declared_attr
41	    def tenant_id(cls) -> Mapped[uuid.UUID]:
42	        return mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False, index=True)

45	class AuditMixin:
46	    """Marker mixin (D-010): tags a model for split-phase audit capture. It adds NO
47	    columns — the audit listeners in core/audit.py test ``isinstance(obj, AuditMixin)``
48	    to decide which INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE flushes land in core_audit_log. Per-column
49	    opt-outs are declared on the model via ``__audit_exclude__`` (a frozenset of
50	    attribute names); ``password_hash`` is excluded there on User."""

53	    # override by setting their own frozenset; the listeners read it via getattr.
54	    __audit_exclude__: frozenset[str] = frozenset()

57	def utcnow() -> datetime:

63	    """Timezone-aware UTC stamps, ALWAYS Python-written (#34).
64	
65	    The Python ``default``/``onupdate`` fire for ORM and Core inserts alike, so every
66	    stored value uses SQLAlchemy's canonical SQLite string format (six-digit
67	    microseconds). The DDL ``server_default`` remains only as a fallback for raw SQL
68	    outside SQLAlchemy and must never be relied on: SQLite's CURRENT_TIMESTAMP writes
69	    second-precision strings whose lexicographic comparison against bound datetimes
70	    breaks keyset-pagination equality — the #34 infinite-page-loop bug."""

72	    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
73	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True),

87	def tenant_fk(target_table: str, local_column: str | None = None) -> sa.ForeignKeyConstraint:
88	    """Tenant-safe foreign key for __table_args__ (D-007 item 4).

98	    return sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
99	        ["tenant_id", local_column],
100	        [f"{target_table}.tenant_id", f"{target_table}.id"],

1	"""D-012 document registry, flow links, and chain traversal.
2	
3	The registry turns the polymorphic (doc_type, doc_id) problem into ordinary FK integrity:
4	every business document row links to exactly one ``core_documents`` registry entry via the
5	NOT NULL ``document_id`` FK supplied by ``DocumentMixin``. Predecessor/successor edges live
6	in ``core_doc_links``, so chain traversal is one generic recursive CTE over two narrow
7	tables — the ACDOCA-era Document Relationship Browser shape — with zero module-aware code in
8	core (core imports nothing from modules).
9	
10	Claim-timing (D-012): a document is registered with ``doc_number`` NULL at creation;
11	documents with a draft lifecycle are numbered at posting via the numbering claim, documents
12	permanent at creation are numbered immediately. The partial unique index on
13	``(tenant_id, doc_number)`` is the DB backstop turning any numbering bug into a constraint
14	violation.
15	
16	The ORM models live HERE rather than in core/models.py: models.py is near its ~350-line
17	soft cap, so the D-012 entities sit in their concern file (consistent with numbering.py and
18	sanctioned by the PLAN). Noted in DECISIONS.md.

21	import uuid
22	from dataclasses import dataclass

30	    Base,
31	    TenantMixin,

33	    UuidPKMixin,

35	)

38	# visited-path cycle guard make a malformed graph terminate instead of spinning.
39	_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH = 20

42	class Document(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
43	    """Registry entry for one business document (D-012). ``doc_type`` is a namespaced
44	    constant (``'sales.order'``, ``'finance.journal_entry'``) declared in module
45	    constants.py; ``doc_id`` is the PK of the business row in its own table; ``doc_number``
46	    is assigned at posting (NULL until then); ``status`` is the registry-level status string.
47	
48	    Not AuditMixin: the registry mirrors business rows that are themselves audited — the
49	    document's own table carries the audited business state, so auditing the registry too
50	    would double-record (documented exclusion)."""
51	
52	    __tablename__ = "core_documents"
53	    __table_args__ = (
54	        # One registry row per business document. Explicit name (D-022 convention keys on
55	        # column 0 only and would collide with tenant_unique()).
56	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
57	            "tenant_id", "doc_type", "doc_id", name="uq_core_documents_tenant_id_doc_type_doc_id"
58	        ),
59	        # Required so business rows can reference a registry entry via the composite tenant FK
60	        # (D-007 item 4) — DocumentMixin.document_fk() targets this.
61	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id", name="uq_core_documents_tenant_id"),
62	        # Partial unique index: a tenant may have many UNNUMBERED documents (doc_number NULL)
63	        # but never two with the SAME doc_number. Both dialect kwargs are required — Postgres
64	        # and SQLite each need their own (D-012 / D-021 dialect-kwargs pattern); a plain
65	        # UNIQUE would (incorrectly) reject multiple NULLs on some engines.
66	        sa.Index(
67	            "uq_core_documents_tenant_id_doc_number",
68	            "tenant_id",
69	            "doc_number",
70	            unique=True,

72	            sqlite_where=sa.text("doc_number IS NOT NULL"),
73	        ),
74	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
75	    )

78	    doc_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
79	    doc_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
80	    status: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=True)

83	class DocumentLink(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
84	    """A predecessor -> successor edge between two registry entries (D-012). ``link_type``
85	    names the relationship (``'fulfills'``, ``'invoices'``, ``'reverses'``, ``'posts'``).
86	    Both endpoints carry the composite tenant FK backstop so an edge can never span tenants.
87	    A CHECK forbids self-edges (a document cannot be its own predecessor)."""
88	
89	    __tablename__ = "core_doc_links"
90	    __table_args__ = (
91	        # One edge per (tenant, predecessor, successor). Explicit name (D-022 column-0 rule).
92	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
93	            "tenant_id",
94	            "predecessor_document_id",
95	            "successor_document_id",
96	            name="uq_core_doc_links_tenant_id_predecessor_document_id_successor",
97	        ),
98	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id", name="uq_core_doc_links_tenant_id"),
99	        # Pass the bare token: the D-022 ck convention wraps it as
100	        # ck_<table>_<constraint_name> -> ck_core_doc_links_no_self_link (matches 0006).
101	        sa.CheckConstraint(
102	            "predecessor_document_id != successor_document_id",
103	            name="no_self_link",
104	        ),
105	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
106	        # Both endpoints reference core_documents through the composite tenant FK, so the
107	        # D-022 column-0 convention would name both identically (collision). Spell out
108	        # distinct names that match migration 0006 exactly.
109	        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
110	            ["tenant_id", "predecessor_document_id"],
111	            ["core_documents.tenant_id", "core_documents.id"],
112	            name="fk_core_doc_links_tenant_id_core_documents",
113	        ),
114	        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
115	            ["tenant_id", "successor_document_id"],
116	            ["core_documents.tenant_id", "core_documents.id"],
117	            name="fk_core_doc_links_successor_document_id_core_documents",
118	        ),
119	    )
120	
121	    predecessor_document_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
122	    successor_document_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
123	    link_type: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=True)

126	def document_fk() -> sa.ForeignKeyConstraint:
127	    """Composite tenant-safe FK for a business table's ``document_id`` -> core_documents
128	    (D-007 item 4). A business model that mixes in DocumentMixin adds this to its
129	    __table_args__ so the link can never point at another tenant's registry row, mirroring
130	    the tenant_fk()/tenant_unique() pattern in core/models.py."""
131	    return sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
132	        ["tenant_id", "document_id"],
133	        ["core_documents.tenant_id", "core_documents.id"],
134	    )
135	
136	
137	class DocumentMixin:
138	    """Business-document link mixin (D-012). A business model mixes this in to get a NOT NULL
139	    ``document_id`` column tying its row to its registry entry — so the row CANNOT be inserted
140	    without first registering the document (the dual-write discipline D-012 relies on). The
141	    consuming model must also add ``document_fk()`` to its __table_args__ for the composite
142	    tenant-safe FK (a mixin cannot inject a multi-column FK into the host's __table_args__,
143	    exactly as TenantMixin needs the model to add tenant_fk()). UNIQUE so the registry-to-row
144	    mapping is 1:1.
145	
146	    Usage in a later module model:
147	
148	        class SalesOrder(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, DocumentMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
149	            __tablename__ = "sls_orders"
150	            __table_args__ = (tenant_unique(), tenant_fk("adm_tenants"), document_fk())
151	    """
152	
153	    @declared_attr
154	    def document_id(cls) -> Mapped[uuid.UUID]:
155	        return mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False, unique=True)
156	
157	
158	@dataclass(frozen=True)
159	class ChainNode:
160	    """One document in a flow chain — the registry projection the DocFlowViewer renders."""
161	
162	    document_id: uuid.UUID
163	    doc_type: str
164	    doc_id: uuid.UUID
165	    doc_number: str | None

170	class ChainEdge:
171	    """One predecessor -> successor edge in a flow chain."""
172	
173	    predecessor_document_id: uuid.UUID
174	    successor_document_id: uuid.UUID
175	    link_type: str | None
176	
177	
178	@dataclass(frozen=True)
179	class DocumentChain:
180	    """Full bidirectional flow chain around a document: every connected node plus every edge
181	    among them. Usable directly by the read API (nodes + edges for the viewer)."""
182	
183	    nodes: list[ChainNode]
184	    edges: list[ChainEdge]

187	async def register_document(
188	    session: AsyncSession,
189	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
190	    doc_type: str,
191	    doc_id: uuid.UUID,
192	    *,
193	    doc_number: str | None = None,
194	    status: str | None = None,
195	) -> Document:
196	    """Insert a registry row for a business document and return it (D-012). Called by the
197	    creating service in the same transaction as the business-row insert (the DocumentMixin
198	    NOT NULL FK makes skipping it a hard error). ``doc_number`` is left NULL for draft-
199	    lifecycle documents (numbered later at posting) and set for documents permanent at
200	    creation. A Core insert sets tenant_id explicitly — core/docflow is a D-007 sanctioned
201	    raw-SQL site."""
202	    document_id = uuid.uuid4()
203	    await session.execute(
204	        sa.insert(Document.__table__).values(
205	            id=document_id,
206	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
207	            doc_type=doc_type,
208	            doc_id=doc_id,
209	            doc_number=doc_number,
210	            status=status,
211	        )
212	    )
213	    return (
214	        await session.execute(select(Document).where(Document.id == document_id))
215	    ).scalar_one()
216	
217	
218	async def set_document_status(
219	    session: AsyncSession,
220	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
221	    document_id: uuid.UUID,
222	    *,
223	    status: str | None = None,
224	    doc_number: str | None = None,
225	) -> None:
226	    """Update a registry row's status and/or doc_number in the owning transaction (D-012).
227	
228	    The number is assigned at the moment a draft-lifecycle document becomes permanent (journal
229	    posting) — passing ``doc_number`` here writes it through the partial-unique (tenant,
230	    doc_number) backstop, so any numbering bug surfaces as a constraint violation. Only the
231	    provided arguments are changed (``None`` leaves the column untouched, except doc_number which
232	    is always set when supplied). A Core UPDATE addressed by (tenant_id, id) — a D-007 sanctioned
233	    explicit-tenant raw-SQL site."""
234	    values: dict[str, str | None] = {}
235	    if status is not None:
236	        values["status"] = status
237	    if doc_number is not None:
238	        values["doc_number"] = doc_number
239	    if not values:
240	        return
241	    await session.execute(
242	        sa.update(Document.__table__)
243	        .where(
244	            Document.__table__.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
245	            Document.__table__.c.id == document_id,
246	        )
247	        .values(**values)
248	    )
249	
250	
251	async def link_documents(
252	    session: AsyncSession,
253	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
254	    predecessor: uuid.UUID,
255	    successor: uuid.UUID,
256	    link_type: str | None = None,
257	) -> DocumentLink:
258	    """Create a predecessor -> successor edge and return it (D-012). The UNIQUE(tenant_id,
259	    predecessor, successor) constraint rejects a duplicate edge as an IntegrityError, and
260	    the composite tenant FKs reject endpoints from another tenant. A Core insert sets
261	    tenant_id explicitly (D-007 sanctioned site)."""
262	    link_id = uuid.uuid4()
263	    await session.execute(
264	        sa.insert(DocumentLink.__table__).values(
265	            id=link_id,
266	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
267	            predecessor_document_id=predecessor,
268	            successor_document_id=successor,
269	            link_type=link_type,
270	        )
271	    )
272	    return (
273	        await session.execute(select(DocumentLink).where(DocumentLink.id == link_id))
274	    ).scalar_one()
275	
276	
277	def _build_reachability_cte(
278	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID, start: uuid.UUID, *, forward: bool
279	) -> sa.sql.Selectable:
280	    """One recursive CTE collecting every document reachable from ``start`` in ONE direction.
281	
282	    ``forward=True`` walks successor edges (descendants), ``forward=False`` walks predecessor
283	    edges (ancestors). The recursive member carries a ``depth`` column capped at
284	    _MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH and a ``path`` string of visited ids; the join excludes any node already
285	    on the path, so a diamond or cycle is traversed once and terminates (D-012 visited-path
286	    guard). Works identically on Postgres and SQLite (both support WITH RECURSIVE).
287	    """
288	    links = DocumentLink.__table__
289	    near = links.c.successor_document_id if forward else links.c.predecessor_document_id
290	    far = links.c.predecessor_document_id if forward else links.c.successor_document_id
291	
292	    # Anchor: the start node itself at depth 0. The path representation MUST match how the
293	    # recursive step casts ids (CAST(<Uuid column> AS VARCHAR)), so the start id is cast the
294	    # same way — casting a Uuid-typed literal renders dashless hex on SQLite and dashed on
295	    # PG, exactly as the column cast does, keeping the visited-path guard's LIKE comparison
296	    # apples-to-apples on both engines (a raw str(start) would carry dashes on SQLite and
297	    # silently defeat the guard).
298	    anchor = select(
299	        sa.literal(start, type_=sa.Uuid).label("document_id"),
300	        sa.literal(0).label("depth"),
301	        sa.cast(sa.literal(start, type_=sa.Uuid), sa.String).label("path"),
302	    ).cte("reach", recursive=True)
303	
304	    # Recursive step: from each frontier node, follow edges in the chosen direction to the
305	    # node on the other end, within the tenant, skipping nodes already on the path.
306	    step = (
307	        select(
308	            far.label("document_id"),
309	            (anchor.c.depth + 1).label("depth"),
310	            (anchor.c.path + sa.literal(",") + sa.cast(far, sa.String)).label("path"),
311	        )
312	        .select_from(anchor.join(links, near == anchor.c.document_id))
313	        .where(
314	            links.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
315	            anchor.c.depth < _MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH,
316	            anchor.c.path.notlike(sa.literal("%") + sa.cast(far, sa.String) + sa.literal("%")),
317	        )
318	    )
319	    return anchor.union_all(step)
320	
321	
322	async def get_document_chain(
323	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, document_id: uuid.UUID
324	) -> DocumentChain:
325	    """Traverse the full flow chain around ``document_id`` in BOTH directions and return its
326	    nodes + edges (D-012). Two recursive CTEs (ancestors via predecessor edges, descendants
327	    via successor edges) collect every reachable registry id; their union is the connected
328	    component containing the start node. Edges are the links whose BOTH endpoints fall in that
329	    set. Cycles and diamonds are handled by the per-CTE visited-path guard, so each node and
330	    edge appears once. Returns empty nodes/edges when the id is unknown to this tenant.
331	
332	    Tenant isolation: the CTEs filter links by tenant_id and the registry/edge reads run
333	    under the caller's tenant context (the D-007 ORM filter), so a chain query never returns
334	    another tenant's documents.
335	    """
336	    ancestors = _build_reachability_cte(tenant_id, document_id, forward=False)
337	    descendants = _build_reachability_cte(tenant_id, document_id, forward=True)
338	
339	    ancestor_ids = set(
340	        (await session.execute(select(ancestors.c.document_id))).scalars().all()
341	    )
342	    descendant_ids = set(
343	        (await session.execute(select(descendants.c.document_id))).scalars().all()
344	    )
345	    reachable = ancestor_ids | descendant_ids
346	
347	    # An unknown id reaches only itself; if it is not a real registry row for this tenant,
348	    # there are no nodes to return — surface an empty chain (the router maps that to 404).
349	    document_rows = (
350	        await session.execute(select(Document).where(Document.id.in_(reachable)))
351	    ).scalars().all()
352	    if not document_rows:
353	        return DocumentChain(nodes=[], edges=[])
354	
355	    present_ids = {row.id for row in document_rows}
356	    nodes = [
357	        ChainNode(
358	            document_id=row.id,
359	            doc_type=row.doc_type,
360	            doc_id=row.doc_id,
361	            doc_number=row.doc_number,
362	            status=row.status,
363	        )
364	        for row in document_rows
365	    ]
366	
367	    link_rows = (
368	        await session.execute(
369	            select(DocumentLink).where(
370	                DocumentLink.predecessor_document_id.in_(present_ids),
371	                DocumentLink.successor_document_id.in_(present_ids),
372	            )
373	        )
374	    ).scalars().all()
375	    edges = [
376	        ChainEdge(
377	            predecessor_document_id=link.predecessor_document_id,
378	            successor_document_id=link.successor_document_id,
379	            link_type=link.link_type,
380	        )
381	        for link in link_rows
382	    ]
383	
384	    return DocumentChain(nodes=nodes, edges=edges)
385

1	"""D-012 gapless per-tenant document numbering.
2	
3	One half of the merged registry+numbering subsystem (the other half is core/docflow.py).
4	A document number is claimed INSIDE the business transaction that makes the document
5	permanent (drafts are numbered at posting). Because the counter increment and the
6	document insert commit or roll back together, gaplessness for committed documents falls
7	out of ACID with no burned-number reconciliation state (D-012 claim-timing rule).
8	
9	The atomic claim is a single ``UPDATE core_number_sequences SET next_value = next_value + 1
10	... RETURNING next_value`` — one portable statement that takes the row lock and reads the
11	new counter in one round trip. RETURNING is verified working on the project's aiosqlite
12	(SQLite >= 3.35; this build runs 3.53) and on Postgres, so no SELECT-then-UPDATE fallback
13	is needed (D-012 sanctioned the fallback only if RETURNING were unavailable).
14	
15	The ORM model lives HERE rather than in core/models.py: models.py is at ~273 lines and
16	adding the numbering + docflow entities would push it over the ~350-line soft cap, so the
17	D-012 entities sit in their concern files (numbering.py / docflow.py) — a placement the
18	PLAN sanctions explicitly and STRUCTURE §2 permits ("one concept per file": the sequence
19	concept lives with its claim logic). Noted in DECISIONS.md.
20	"""
21	
22	import uuid
23	from datetime import date
24	
25	import sqlalchemy as sa
26	from sqlalchemy import select
27	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
28	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
29	
30	from app.core.exceptions import NotFoundError
31	from app.core.models import (
32	    Base,
33	    TenantMixin,
34	    TimestampMixin,
35	    UuidPKMixin,
36	    tenant_fk,
37	)
38	
39	
40	class NumberSequence(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
41	    """Per-tenant gapless counter for one document kind (D-012).
42	
43	    ``name`` is the namespaced sequence key (e.g. ``'finance.invoice'``); a claim formats
44	    ``{prefix}-{year?}-{padded next_value}`` (e.g. ``INV-2026-00001``). When ``year_reset``
45	    is set the running number restarts at 1 each calendar year and the year segment is
46	    rendered; ``current_year`` records which year the counter currently belongs to so the
47	    first claim of a new year resets it on demand (no rollover job, per D-012). Not
48	    AuditMixin: sequence rows are infrastructure counters mutated on every claim, not
49	    business state — auditing every increment would be noise (documented exclusion)."""
50	
51	    __tablename__ = "core_number_sequences"
52	    __table_args__ = (
53	        # One sequence per (tenant, name). Explicit name: the D-022 convention keys on
54	        # column 0 (tenant_id) only and would collide with tenant_unique() below.
55	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "name", name="uq_core_number_sequences_tenant_id_name"),
56	        # UNIQUE(tenant_id, id) so other tenant-scoped tables could reference a sequence via
57	        # the composite-FK backstop if ever needed (D-007 item 4).
58	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id", name="uq_core_number_sequences_tenant_id"),
59	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
60	    )
61	
62	    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(100), nullable=False)
63	    prefix: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(20), nullable=False)
64	    padding: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False)
65	    # Next number to hand out. The atomic claim does next_value = next_value + 1 RETURNING
66	    # the post-increment value, so the FIRST claim of a sequence at next_value=1 returns 1.
67	    next_value: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
68	        sa.Integer, nullable=False, default=1, server_default=sa.text("1")
69	    )
70	    year_reset: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
71	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=False, server_default=sa.false()
72	    )
73	    # The year the running counter belongs to (NULL when year_reset is off).
74	    current_year: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=True)
75	
76	
77	def _format_number(prefix: str, padding: int, value: int, year: int | None) -> str:
78	    """Render ``{prefix}-{year?}-{padded value}`` — the year segment is present only when
79	    the sequence year-resets (D-012). e.g. ('INV', 5, 1, 2026) -> 'INV-2026-00001'."""
80	    padded = str(value).zfill(padding)
81	    if year is None:
82	        return f"{prefix}-{padded}"
83	    return f"{prefix}-{year}-{padded}"
84	
85	
86	async def ensure_sequence(
87	    session: AsyncSession,
88	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
89	    name: str,
90	    prefix: str,
91	    padding: int,
92	    year_reset: bool,
93	) -> NumberSequence:
94	    """Idempotent creator for provisioning/seed (D-012: year rollover and sequence setup
95	    need no job — the row is created on demand). Returns the existing row unchanged if the
96	    (tenant, name) sequence already exists, otherwise inserts it at next_value=1.
97	
98	    A Core insert is used (not an ORM add) so the tenant_id is set explicitly and the row
99	    is not subject to ORM tenant stamping — consistent with the D-007 sanction that core/
100	    numbering writes carry tenant_id explicitly. Callers run under the target tenant context
101	    or system_context (provisioning)."""
102	    existing = (
103	        await session.execute(
104	            select(NumberSequence).where(
105	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == name
106	            )
107	        )
108	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
109	    if existing is not None:
110	        return existing
111	
112	    current_year = date.today().year if year_reset else None
113	    await session.execute(
114	        sa.insert(NumberSequence.__table__).values(
115	            id=uuid.uuid4(),
116	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
117	            name=name,
118	            prefix=prefix,
119	            padding=padding,
120	            next_value=1,
121	            year_reset=year_reset,
122	            current_year=current_year,
123	        )
124	    )
125	    return (
126	        await session.execute(
127	            select(NumberSequence).where(
128	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == name
129	            )
130	        )
131	    ).scalar_one()
132	
133	
134	async def claim_number(
135	    session: AsyncSession,
136	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
137	    sequence_name: str,
138	    *,
139	    on_date: date,
140	) -> str:
141	    """Atomically claim the next number for ``sequence_name`` and return the formatted
142	    string (D-012). The claim runs in the CALLER's transaction — the number is permanent
143	    only when that transaction commits, so a rollback returns the value to the pool and the
144	    next committed claim reuses it (gaplessness for committed documents).
145	
146	    Mechanism — one portable atomic statement per claim:
147	    ``UPDATE core_number_sequences SET next_value = next_value + 1
148	      WHERE tenant_id=:t AND name=:n RETURNING next_value`` — the RETURNING value is the
149	    post-increment counter; the row lock the UPDATE takes serializes concurrent claimers so
150	    two claims can never read the same number (verified on aiosqlite >= 3.35 and Postgres).
151	
152	    Year reset (when ``year_reset``): if ``on_date.year`` differs from the stored
153	    ``current_year``, the counter is reset to 1 for the new year FIRST (a guarded UPDATE
154	    that only fires while current_year is still the old value, so a concurrent claimer that
155	    reset it already cannot double-reset), then the normal atomic increment claims 1.
156	
157	    A Core UPDATE is used (bypasses the ORM tenant filter by design — core/ numbering is a
158	    D-007 sanctioned raw-SQL site with explicit tenant_id)."""
159	    sequence = (
160	        await session.execute(
161	            select(NumberSequence).where(
162	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == sequence_name
163	            )
164	        )
165	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
166	    if sequence is None:
167	        raise NotFoundError(
168	            message=f"Number sequence '{sequence_name}' is not configured for this tenant",
169	            code="core.number_sequence_missing",
170	        )
171	
172	    table = NumberSequence.__table__
173	    claim_year: int | None = None
174	    if sequence.year_reset:
175	        claim_year = on_date.year
176	        if sequence.current_year != claim_year:
177	            # Reset to 1 for the new year, guarded on the OLD current_year so a racing
178	            # claimer that already rolled the year over does not reset a second time.
179	            await session.execute(
180	                sa.update(table)
181	                .where(
182	                    table.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
183	                    table.c.name == sequence_name,
184	                    table.c.current_year.is_not_distinct_from(sequence.current_year),
185	                )
186	                .values(next_value=1, current_year=claim_year)
187	            )
188	
189	    result = await session.execute(
190	        sa.update(table)
191	        .where(table.c.tenant_id == tenant_id, table.c.name == sequence_name)
192	        .values(next_value=table.c.next_value + 1)
193	        .returning(table.c.next_value)
194	    )
195	    next_after = result.scalar_one()
196	    claimed_value = next_after - 1
197	
198	    # The Core UPDATE changed the row out from under the loaded ORM object; expire it so its
199	    # attributes reload from the DB on next access rather than being marked dirty (which
200	    # would trigger a redundant ORM UPDATE on the next flush).
201	    formatted = _format_number(sequence.prefix, sequence.padding, claimed_value, claim_year)
202	    session.expire(sequence)
203	    return formatted
