1	"""RBAC engine (D-009): code-defined permission catalog, permission resolution with a
2	short TTL cache, the require_permission dependency factory, and field-level read masking.
3	
4	The catalog is the source of truth: modules declare their permission keys in their
5	``constants.py`` and register them here at import time via ``register_permissions``;
6	``sync_permission_catalog`` upserts the registry into ``core_permissions`` so tenants
7	can only ever be granted keys that some code path actually checks. Roles and grants are
8	tenant data (core/models.py); resolution joins user_roles -> role_permissions ->
9	permissions in one query, memoized 60s keyed on (tenant_id, user_id, token_version).
10	"""
11	
12	import functools
13	import time
14	import uuid
15	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
16	from contextvars import ContextVar
17	from typing import Annotated, Any
18	
19	from fastapi import Depends
20	from pydantic import WrapSerializer
21	from pydantic_core.core_schema import SerializerFunctionWrapHandler
22	from sqlalchemy import select
23	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
24	
25	from app.core.exceptions import PermissionDeniedError
26	from app.core.models import Permission, RolePermission, UserRole
27	
28	# --- Permission catalog (code-defined source of truth) ------------------------
29	
30	# Module-level registry. Modules call register_permissions at import; the values are
31	# the human-readable descriptions seeded alongside the key. Insertion-ordered so the
32	# catalog sync and tests see a stable order.
33	_CATALOG: dict[str, str | None] = {}
34	
35	
36	def register_permissions(*keys: str, descriptions: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> None:
37	    """Declare permission keys that exist in code (D-009). Idempotent: re-registering a
38	    key keeps the first description unless a new one is supplied. Modules call this at
39	    import from their ``constants.py`` (e.g. ``register_permissions(FIN_JOURNAL_POST)``)."""
40	    descriptions = descriptions or {}
41	    for key in keys:
42	        new_description = descriptions.get(key)
43	        if key not in _CATALOG or new_description is not None:
44	            _CATALOG[key] = new_description if new_description is not None else _CATALOG.get(key)
45	
46	
47	def catalog_keys() -> frozenset[str]:
48	    """The full set of code-declared permission keys (the grantable universe)."""
49	    return frozenset(_CATALOG)
50	
51	
52	# Core permission keys, registered at import (module __init__ files register theirs).
53	# Format is ``module.entity.action`` per STRUCTURE §7.
54	ADMIN_USER_MANAGE = "admin.user.manage"
55	ADMIN_ROLE_MANAGE = "admin.role.manage"
56	ADMIN_AUDIT_READ = "admin.audit.read"
57	ADMIN_TENANT_MANAGE = "admin.tenant.manage"
58	CORE_DOCUMENT_READ = "core.document.read"
59	CORE_SETTING_MANAGE = "core.setting.manage"
60	
61	register_permissions(
62	    ADMIN_USER_MANAGE,
63	    ADMIN_ROLE_MANAGE,
64	    ADMIN_AUDIT_READ,
65	    ADMIN_TENANT_MANAGE,
66	    CORE_DOCUMENT_READ,
67	    CORE_SETTING_MANAGE,
68	    descriptions={
69	        ADMIN_USER_MANAGE: "Create, edit and deactivate users",
70	        ADMIN_ROLE_MANAGE: "Create roles and assign permissions",
71	        ADMIN_AUDIT_READ: "Read the audit log",
72	        ADMIN_TENANT_MANAGE: "Manage tenant settings and provisioning",
73	        CORE_DOCUMENT_READ: "View documents and their flow",
74	        CORE_SETTING_MANAGE: "Manage tenant-level configuration",
75	    },
76	)
77	
78	
79	async def sync_permission_catalog(session: AsyncSession) -> int:
80	    """Upsert every code-declared key into core_permissions (D-009). Idempotent: existing
81	    keys are left as-is, only missing ones are inserted, so re-running creates no dupes.
82	    Permissions are GLOBAL data — callers run this under system_context (seed/provisioning).
83	    Returns the number of rows inserted this call."""
84	    existing = set(
85	        (await session.execute(select(Permission.key))).scalars().all()
86	    )
87	    inserted = 0
88	    for key, description in _CATALOG.items():
89	        if key in existing:
90	            continue
91	        session.add(Permission(key=key, description=description))
92	        inserted += 1
93	    await session.flush()
94	    return inserted
95	
96	
97	# --- Permission resolution + TTL cache (D-009) --------------------------------
98	
99	_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 60.0
100	# key -> (expires_at_monotonic, permissions). Process-local; multi-worker deploys lag
101	# per worker by at most the TTL, or instantly on token_version bump (the key changes).
102	_CACHE: dict[tuple[uuid.UUID, uuid.UUID, int], tuple[float, frozenset[str]]] = {}
103	
104	
105	def clear_cache() -> None:
106	    """Drop every cached resolution. Used by tests and a future global flush."""
107	    _CACHE.clear()
108	
109	
110	def invalidate(tenant_id: uuid.UUID, user_id: uuid.UUID, token_version: int) -> None:
111	    """Evict one principal's cached permissions after a role change (D-009). Callers that
112	    only know (tenant, user) can pass any token_version they hold; on mismatch the stale
113	    entry simply expires within the TTL — but admin role mutations should pass the live
114	    token_version so the next request recomputes immediately."""
115	    _CACHE.pop((tenant_id, user_id, token_version), None)
116	
117	
118	async def _query_permissions(
119	    session: AsyncSession, user_id: uuid.UUID, tenant_id: uuid.UUID
120	) -> frozenset[str]:
121	    """ONE join: user_roles -> role_permissions -> permissions -> effective key set.
122	    Runs under the request's tenant context, so the user_roles/role_permissions rows are
123	    already tenant-filtered; the explicit user_id predicate narrows to this principal."""
124	    stmt = (
125	        select(Permission.key)
126	        .select_from(UserRole)
127	        .join(RolePermission, RolePermission.role_id == UserRole.role_id)
128	        .join(Permission, Permission.id == RolePermission.permission_id)
129	        .where(UserRole.user_id == user_id)
130	        .distinct()
131	    )
132	    keys = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all()
133	    return frozenset(keys)
134	
135	
136	async def resolve_permissions(
137	    session: AsyncSession,
138	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
139	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
140	    token_version: int,
141	    now: float | None = None,
142	) -> frozenset[str]:
143	    """Effective permission set for a principal, memoized 60s (D-009). ``now`` is an
144	    optional monotonic timestamp for deterministic tests; production uses time.monotonic.
145	    Tests prefer clear_cache()/invalidate() over advancing the clock."""
146	    clock = now if now is not None else time.monotonic()
147	    cache_key = (tenant_id, user_id, token_version)
148	    cached = _CACHE.get(cache_key)
149	    if cached is not None and cached[0] > clock:
150	        return cached[1]
151	    permissions = await _query_permissions(session, user_id, tenant_id)
152	    _CACHE[cache_key] = (clock + _CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, permissions)
153	    return permissions
154	
155	
156	# --- require_permission dependency factory (D-009) ----------------------------
157	
158	
159	def require_permission(key: str) -> Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]]:
160	    """FastAPI dependency factory: returns a dependency that loads the current principal
161	    (reusing get_current_user) and raises PermissionDeniedError (403, code
162	    ``rbac.permission_denied``, details naming the missing key) unless ``key`` is in the
163	    principal's resolved permissions. Attach per route via
164	    ``dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(ADMIN_USER_MANAGE))]``."""
165	
166	    # Imported here, not at module top, to avoid a core import cycle: deps imports rbac
167	    # (get_current_user resolves permissions) and rbac imports deps (this guard).
168	    from app.core.deps import CurrentUser, get_current_user
169	
170	    async def _dependency(
171	        current: Annotated[CurrentUser, Depends(get_current_user)],
172	    ) -> CurrentUser:
173	        if key not in current.permissions:
174	            raise PermissionDeniedError(
175	                code="rbac.permission_denied",
176	                message=f"Missing permission: {key}",
177	                details={"permission": key},
178	            )
179	        return current
180	
181	    return _dependency
182	
183	
184	# --- Field-level read masking (D-009) -----------------------------------------
185	
186	# Serialization-time principal permissions. Set by get_current_user per request and by
187	# the test ``permissions_context`` fixture; default empty so anything serialized OUTSIDE
188	# a request (jobs, tests without the fixture) fails CLOSED — masked fields read as None.
189	current_permissions: ContextVar[frozenset[str]] = ContextVar(
190	    "current_permissions", default=frozenset()
191	)
192	
193	def _mask_serializer(
194	    permission: str, value: Any, handler: SerializerFunctionWrapHandler
195	) -> Any:
196	    """WrapSerializer body (D-009): emit the real serialized value only when the guarding
197	    permission is present in current_permissions, else None. The permission is bound via
198	    functools.partial below — a WrapSerializer cannot read loose Annotated metadata."""
199	    if permission in current_permissions.get():
200	        return handler(value)
201	    return None
202	
203	
204	def Masked[T](tp: type[T], permission: str) -> Any:  # noqa: N802 - type-factory, PascalCase by design
205	    """Annotate a Pydantic field as read-masked behind ``permission`` (D-009).
206	
207	    Usage::
208	
209	        class EmployeeRead(ApiModel):
210	            base_salary: Masked(Decimal | None, "hr.compensation.read")
211	
212	    Serializes to the real value when current_permissions contains the key, else None.
213	    CONVENTION: masked fields are EXCLUDED from the entity's Create/Update schemas and
214	    edited through a separate permission-guarded endpoint, so a partial update can never
215	    silently null a masked field (the HR module enforces this for compensation)."""
216	    return Annotated[
217	        tp | None,
218	        WrapSerializer(functools.partial(_mask_serializer, permission)),
219	    ]
220

1	"""D-014 keyset (seek) pagination — never OFFSET.
2	
3	Cursor browsing is O(page) at any depth and stable under concurrent inserts (the ERP norm for
4	ledger/list browsing). Every list orders by a whitelisted sort column plus the PK ``id`` as a
5	mandatory unique tiebreaker (``ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC``), fetches ``limit + 1`` rows,
6	and emits ``next_cursor`` from the last RETURNED row only when the extra row arrived.
7	
8	**Cursor.** ``base64url(JSON)`` of ``{"v":1, "k":[last sort values..., last id], "s": sort-spec,
9	"q": filter fingerprint}`` — opaque to clients, validated server-side. ``v``, ``s`` and ``q`` must
10	match the current request (a cursor minted for one query/sort/filter can't be replayed on
11	another) → 400 ``pagination.invalid_cursor`` on any mismatch or tamper.
12	
13	**Seek predicate.** Written in the EXPANDED portable OR-form
14	``col0 < k0 OR (col0 = k0 AND col1 < k1) OR (... AND id < kN)`` (directions flipped per column for
15	ASC). D-014 mandates this expansion because SQLite lacks MIXED-direction row-value comparison —
16	``(a, b) > (x, y)`` only works when every column sorts the same way, and our lists mix ASC/DESC
17	freely — so the expansion is the only form correct on BOTH engines (verified: this project's
18	aiosqlite, 3.53, DOES support uniform-direction row-values, but the expanded form is used
19	unconditionally so a mixed-direction sort is never silently wrong).
20	
21	**Placement deviation.** D-014's letter puts ``paginate`` in ``core/db.py`` and the cursor codec
22	in ``core/schemas.py``. The keyset machinery (codec + fingerprint + expanded predicate +
23	CursorParams) is substantial and cross-cutting, so it gets its own flat core file per STRUCTURE
24	§8.5 ("one concept per file") — a justified core addition recorded in DECISIONS.md, the same way
25	core/money.py and core/custom_fields.py were. The ``Page`` envelope stays in core/schemas.py.
26	"""
27	
28	import base64
29	import binascii
30	import hashlib
31	import json
32	import uuid
33	from dataclasses import dataclass
34	from datetime import date, datetime
35	from decimal import Decimal
36	from enum import StrEnum
37	from typing import Any
38	
39	import sqlalchemy as sa
40	from pydantic import BaseModel
41	from sqlalchemy import Select
42	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
43	from sqlalchemy.orm import InstrumentedAttribute
44	
45	from app.core.exceptions import ValidationFailedError
46	from app.core.schemas import Page
47	
48	DEFAULT_LIMIT = 50
49	MAX_LIMIT = 200
50	_CURSOR_VERSION = 1
51	
52	
53	class SortDirection(StrEnum):
54	    ASC = "asc"
55	    DESC = "desc"
56	
57	
58	@dataclass(frozen=True)
59	class OrderKey:
60	    """One whitelisted sort column + direction. ``paginate`` always appends the PK as the final
61	    tiebreaker, so a list declares only its business sort columns (e.g. created_at DESC)."""
62	
63	    column: InstrumentedAttribute[Any]
64	    direction: SortDirection = SortDirection.ASC
65	
66	    @property
67	    def name(self) -> str:
68	        return self.column.key
69	
70	
71	def _sort_spec(order_keys: list[OrderKey]) -> str:
72	    """Stable string identity of the sort (``'created_at:desc,id:asc'``), embedded in the cursor
73	    so a cursor minted under one ordering is rejected if the request's ordering changed."""
74	    return ",".join(f"{key.name}:{key.direction.value}" for key in order_keys)
75	
76	
77	def _encode_value(value: Any) -> Any:
78	    """Serialize a sort-key value to a JSON-safe, round-trippable form. datetimes/dates go to ISO
79	    strings, Decimals to strings (exact, consistent with D-015), UUIDs to str; primitives pass."""
80	    if isinstance(value, datetime | date):
81	        return value.isoformat()
82	    if isinstance(value, Decimal):
83	        return str(value)
84	    if isinstance(value, bool | int | float | str) or value is None:
85	        return value
86	    return str(value)
87	
88	
89	def encode_cursor(key_values: list[Any], sort_spec: str, filter_fingerprint: str) -> str:
90	    """base64url(JSON) of the last row's key tuple + the sort/filter fingerprints (D-014)."""
91	    payload = {
92	        "v": _CURSOR_VERSION,
93	        "k": [_encode_value(value) for value in key_values],
94	        "s": sort_spec,
95	        "q": filter_fingerprint,
96	    }
97	    raw = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
98	    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).decode("ascii")
99	
100	
101	def decode_cursor(cursor: str, sort_spec: str, filter_fingerprint: str) -> list[Any]:
102	    """Decode and validate a cursor, returning its key tuple. Any tamper, malformed payload, wrong
103	    version, or a sort/filter fingerprint that does not match the CURRENT request raises 400
104	    ``pagination.invalid_cursor`` — a cursor cannot be replayed on a different query (D-014)."""
105	    try:
106	        raw = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(cursor.encode("ascii"))
107	        payload = json.loads(raw)
108	    except (binascii.Error, ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
109	        raise _invalid_cursor() from exc
110	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
111	        raise _invalid_cursor()
112	    if (
113	        payload.get("v") != _CURSOR_VERSION
114	        or payload.get("s") != sort_spec
115	        or payload.get("q") != filter_fingerprint
116	        or not isinstance(payload.get("k"), list)
117	    ):
118	        raise _invalid_cursor()
119	    return payload["k"]
120	
121	
122	def _invalid_cursor() -> ValidationFailedError:
123	    return ValidationFailedError(
124	        message="The pagination cursor is invalid for this query",
125	        code="pagination.invalid_cursor",
126	    )
127	
128	
129	def filter_fingerprint(*parts: Any) -> str:
130	    """sha256-prefix of normalized filter parts (D-014). Routers pass whatever WHERE inputs scope
131	    the list (status, date range, search term…); a different filter set yields a different
132	    fingerprint, so a cursor from one filtered view can't bleed into another. Empty parts → the
133	    fingerprint of an empty filter set, still stable."""
134	    canonical = json.dumps([_encode_value(part) for part in parts], separators=(",", ":"))
135	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
136	
137	
138	def _coerce_key_value(column: InstrumentedAttribute[Any], value: Any) -> Any:
139	    """Coerce a decoded cursor value back to the column's Python type so the seek comparison binds
140	    correctly on both engines. datetimes/dates and Decimals were ISO/str-encoded; the rest are
141	    JSON primitives that bind as-is (SQLAlchemy adapts UUID/str columns from the str form)."""
142	    python_type = getattr(column.type, "python_type", None)
143	    if value is None or python_type is None or not isinstance(value, str):
144	        return value
145	    if python_type is datetime:
146	        return datetime.fromisoformat(value)
147	    if python_type is date:
148	        return date.fromisoformat(value)
149	    if python_type is Decimal:
150	        return Decimal(value)
151	    if python_type is uuid.UUID:
152	        # The PK tiebreaker is a UUID column; SQLAlchemy's Uuid type binds a uuid.UUID, not the
153	        # str it was cursor-encoded as, so re-parse it here (else the bind processor blows up).
154	        return uuid.UUID(value)
155	    return value
156	
157	
158	def _seek_predicate(order_keys: list[OrderKey], key_values: list[Any]) -> sa.ColumnElement[bool]:
159	    """Build the expanded OR-form seek predicate (D-014). For sort columns c0..cN with the values
160	    from the previous page's last row, the predicate selecting STRICTLY-AFTER rows is::
161	
162	        cmp(c0)
163	        OR (c0 == v0 AND cmp(c1))
164	        OR (c0 == v0 AND c1 == v1 AND cmp(c2))
165	        ...
166	
167	    where ``cmp`` is ``<`` for a DESC column and ``>`` for ASC. The PK tiebreaker is already the
168	    last OrderKey, so every distinct row is on exactly one side of the boundary — no skips, no
169	    duplicates, even when earlier sort columns tie. Expanded (not row-value) so mixed ASC/DESC is
170	    correct on SQLite too."""
171	    coerced = [
172	        _coerce_key_value(key.column, value)
173	        for key, value in zip(order_keys, key_values, strict=True)
174	    ]
175	    clauses: list[sa.ColumnElement[bool]] = []
176	    for i, key in enumerate(order_keys):
177	        equals = [order_keys[j].column == coerced[j] for j in range(i)]
178	        strict = (
179	            key.column > coerced[i]
180	            if key.direction is SortDirection.ASC
181	            else key.column < coerced[i]
182	        )
183	        clauses.append(sa.and_(*equals, strict))
184	    return sa.or_(*clauses)
185	
186	
187	def _apply_order(stmt: Select[Any], order_keys: list[OrderKey]) -> Select[Any]:
188	    return stmt.order_by(
189	        *(
190	            key.column.asc() if key.direction is SortDirection.ASC else key.column.desc()
191	            for key in order_keys
192	        )
193	    )
194	
195	
196	async def paginate[T](
197	    session: AsyncSession,
198	    stmt: Select[tuple[T]],
199	    *,
200	    order_by: list[OrderKey],
201	    pk: InstrumentedAttribute[Any],
202	    cursor: str | None = None,
203	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
204	    filters: str = "",
205	) -> Page[T]:
206	    """Keyset-paginate ``stmt`` and return a ``Page[T]`` (D-014). ``order_by`` is the whitelisted
207	    business sort; ``pk`` (the model's id) is appended as the mandatory unique tiebreaker so the
208	    cursor is stable. ``filters`` is the router's filter fingerprint (see
209	    :func:`filter_fingerprint`) baked into the cursor. The single generic helper module routers
210	    use — they never hand-roll keyset SQL.
211	
212	    Fetches ``limit + 1`` rows; if the extra row arrives, the page is full and ``next_cursor`` is
213	    minted from the LAST returned row's sort-key tuple. The cursor (when present) is decoded and
214	    validated against this request's sort + filter fingerprint, then turned into the expanded-OR
215	    seek predicate that selects strictly-after rows."""
216	    if limit < 1:
217	        limit = 1
218	    keys = [*order_by, OrderKey(pk, SortDirection.ASC)]
219	    sort_spec = _sort_spec(keys)
220	
221	    seek_stmt = stmt
222	    if cursor is not None:
223	        key_values = decode_cursor(cursor, sort_spec, filters)
224	        if len(key_values) != len(keys):
225	            raise _invalid_cursor()
226	        seek_stmt = seek_stmt.where(_seek_predicate(keys, key_values))
227	
228	    seek_stmt = _apply_order(seek_stmt, keys).limit(limit + 1)
229	    rows = list((await session.execute(seek_stmt)).scalars().all())
230	
231	    has_more = len(rows) > limit
232	    items = rows[:limit]
233	    next_cursor: str | None = None
234	    if has_more and items:
235	        last = items[-1]
236	        next_cursor = encode_cursor(
237	            [getattr(last, key.name) for key in keys], sort_spec, filters
238	        )
239	    return Page(items=items, next_cursor=next_cursor, limit=limit)
240	
241	
242	def map_page[S: BaseModel](page: Page[Any], schema: type[S]) -> Page[S]:
243	    """Validate a service-layer ``Page`` of ORM rows into its wire schema — the one-line router
244	    epilogue for every paginated list endpoint, so the items/next_cursor/limit plumbing is never
245	    hand-rolled (and the envelope can't drift between endpoints)."""
246	    return Page(
247	        items=[schema.model_validate(item) for item in page.items],
248	        next_cursor=page.next_cursor,
249	        limit=page.limit,
250	    )
251	
252	
253	@dataclass(frozen=True)
254	class CursorParams:
255	    """Parsed ``?cursor=&limit=`` query params (D-014). ``limit`` is clamped to ``[1, MAX_LIMIT]``
256	    and defaults to ``DEFAULT_LIMIT``, so a client can never request an unbounded page. A router
257	    declares ``params: CursorParamsDep`` and forwards ``params.cursor`` / ``params.limit`` to
258	    :func:`paginate`."""
259	
260	    cursor: str | None
261	    limit: int
262	
263	
264	def cursor_params(cursor: str | None = None, limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT) -> CursorParams:
265	    """FastAPI dependency parsing the cursor/limit query params with the max-limit cap (D-014)."""
266	    clamped = max(1, min(limit, MAX_LIMIT))
267	    return CursorParams(cursor=cursor, limit=clamped)
268	
269	
270	__all__ = [
271	    "DEFAULT_LIMIT",
272	    "MAX_LIMIT",
273	    "CursorParams",
274	    "OrderKey",
275	    "SortDirection",
276	    "cursor_params",
277	    "decode_cursor",
278	    "encode_cursor",
279	    "filter_fingerprint",
280	    "map_page",
281	    "paginate",
282	]

1	"""FastAPI dependencies (D-008 get_current_user, D-007 production ContextVar setter).
2	
3	This is the ONE place that sets `current_tenant_id` for the request lifecycle from a
4	validated access token; the pure-ASGI middleware in app.main resets it in a finally
5	block so request A's tenant never leaks to request B on the same worker.
6	"""
7	
8	import uuid
9	from dataclasses import dataclass
10	from typing import Annotated
11	
12	from fastapi import Depends
13	from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
14	from sqlalchemy import select
15	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker
16	
17	from app.core.audit import actor_user_id_ctx
18	from app.core.auth import decode_token
19	from app.core.config import get_settings
20	from app.core.db import get_session, get_session_factory
21	from app.core.exceptions import AuthError
22	from app.core.models import User
23	from app.core.rbac import current_permissions, resolve_permissions
24	from app.core.tenancy import current_tenant_id
25	
26	# get_session / get_settings are re-exported so routers depend on a single core.deps
27	# surface rather than reaching into core.db / core.config directly.
28	__all__ = [
29	    "CurrentUser",
30	    "CurrentUserDep",
31	    "SessionDep",
32	    "SessionFactoryDep",
33	    "get_current_user",
34	    "get_session",
35	    "get_session_factory",
36	    "get_settings",
37	]
38	
39	# auto_error=False: a missing/blank header must surface as the D-014 auth envelope
40	# (AuthError -> 401), not Starlette's bare 403 HTTPException.
41	_bearer_scheme = HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)
42	
43	# Annotated dependency aliases: the modern FastAPI idiom that keeps Depends() out of
44	# parameter defaults (ruff B008) and lets routers share one typed handle.
45	SessionDep = Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_session)]
46	# The sessionmaker dependency (test-overridable like get_session). Job-submitting routers pass
47	# it to schedule_job post-commit so the runner opens its sessions against the SAME database —
48	# the app factory in production, the per-test engine's factory under the conftest override.
49	SessionFactoryDep = Annotated[async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession], Depends(get_session_factory)]
50	_CredentialsDep = Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None, Depends(_bearer_scheme)]
51	
52	
53	@dataclass(frozen=True)
54	class CurrentUser:
55	    """Resolved request principal (D-008/D-009). `permissions` is the effective key set
56	    resolved by RBAC (one join query, cached 60s)."""
57	
58	    user_id: uuid.UUID
59	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID
60	    permissions: frozenset[str]
61	    token_version: int
62	
63	
64	async def get_current_user(
65	    credentials: _CredentialsDep,
66	    session: SessionDep,
67	) -> CurrentUser:
68	    if credentials is None:
69	        raise AuthError(message="Missing bearer token", code="auth.invalid_token")
70	
71	    claims = decode_token(credentials.credentials, expected_typ="access")
72	    try:
73	        user_id = uuid.UUID(claims["sub"])
74	        tenant_id = uuid.UUID(claims["tenant_id"])
75	        claim_version = int(claims["ver"])
76	    except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
77	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token") from exc
78	
79	    # Set the tenancy ContextVar FROM the validated token (D-007 production setter):
80	    # the user lookup below then runs under the token's tenant, so a tampered
81	    # tenant_id can only ever resolve a user that actually belongs to that tenant —
82	    # cross-tenant access is impossible. The middleware resets this in a finally block.
83	    current_tenant_id.set(tenant_id)
84	
85	    user = (
86	        await session.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
87	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
88	    if user is None or not user.is_active:
89	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token")
90	    if user.token_version != claim_version:
91	        # Stale token after a "revoke everything" bump (D-008).
92	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token")
93	
94	    # RBAC resolution (D-009): one join query, memoized 60s on
95	    # (tenant_id, user_id, token_version). Runs under the tenant context set above, so
96	    # the user_roles/role_permissions rows are already tenant-filtered.
97	    permissions = await resolve_permissions(
98	        session, user.id, user.tenant_id, user.token_version
99	    )
100	    # Serialization-time masking (D-009) reads this ContextVar; the middleware resets it
101	    # in a finally block alongside current_tenant_id so it never leaks across requests.
102	    current_permissions.set(permissions)
103	    # D-010 audit context: now that the principal is known, stamp the actor onto every
104	    # audit row this request writes. The middleware seeded it None (system) and resets it.
105	    actor_user_id_ctx.set(user.id)
106	
107	    return CurrentUser(
108	        user_id=user.id,
109	        tenant_id=user.tenant_id,
110	        permissions=permissions,
111	        token_version=user.token_version,
112	    )
113	
114	
115	CurrentUserDep = Annotated[CurrentUser, Depends(get_current_user)]
116

1	"""AtlasError hierarchy rendered as the D-014 error envelope by handlers in app.main.
2	
3	This file also owns the D-014 DB-guard translation: trigger-raised `ATLAS_*` tokens are
4	mapped to envelope codes here so the DB backstops surface through the SAME envelope as
5	service-level checks. Kept in this file (not a new core/db_errors.py) because the map is a
6	small dict and STRUCTURE §8.1 prefers extending an existing home; promote to its own file
7	only if the table grows past a screenful.
8	"""
9	
10	from typing import Any
11	
12	from sqlalchemy.exc import DBAPIError
13	
14	
15	class AtlasError(Exception):
16	    """Base for every error the API surfaces deliberately. Codes are machine-readable
17	    and dot-namespaced (generic: common.*; domain rules: e.g. finance.period_closed)."""
18	
19	    def __init__(
20	        self,
21	        code: str,
22	        message: str,
23	        status_code: int = 400,
24	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
25	    ) -> None:
26	        super().__init__(message)
27	        self.code = code
28	        self.message = message
29	        self.status_code = status_code
30	        self.details = details
31	
32	
33	class NotFoundError(AtlasError):
34	    def __init__(
35	        self,
36	        message: str = "Resource not found",
37	        code: str = "common.not_found",
38	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
39	    ) -> None:
40	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=404, details=details)
41	
42	
43	class ValidationFailedError(AtlasError):
44	    def __init__(
45	        self,
46	        message: str = "Validation failed",
47	        code: str = "common.validation_error",
48	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
49	    ) -> None:
50	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=422, details=details)
51	
52	
53	class ConflictError(AtlasError):
54	    def __init__(
55	        self,
56	        message: str = "Conflict with existing state",
57	        code: str = "common.conflict",
58	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
59	    ) -> None:
60	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=409, details=details)
61	
62	
63	class AuthError(AtlasError):
64	    def __init__(
65	        self,
66	        message: str = "Invalid credentials",
67	        code: str = "auth.invalid_credentials",
68	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
69	    ) -> None:
70	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=401, details=details)
71	
72	
73	class PermissionDeniedError(AtlasError):
74	    def __init__(
75	        self,
76	        message: str = "Permission denied",
77	        code: str = "common.permission_denied",
78	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
79	    ) -> None:
80	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=403, details=details)
81	
82	
83	class TenancyError(AtlasError):
84	    def __init__(
85	        self,
86	        message: str = "Tenant context missing or mismatched",
87	        code: str = "tenancy.context_missing",
88	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
89	    ) -> None:
90	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=403, details=details)
91	
92	
93	# --- D-014 DB-guard translation (trigger token -> envelope) --------------------
94	#
95	# Table-driven so future backstops (ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED, ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE,
96	# ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY) plug in by adding one row. SQLite RAISE(ABORT) surfaces as
97	# IntegrityError and asyncpg plpgsql RAISE surfaces differently, but both are subclasses
98	# of DBAPIError and both carry the token in str(exc) — so substring matching on the base
99	# class covers both engines (D-022 pins it on each).
100	#
101	# DEVIATION from D-014's literal table: D-014 maps ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY ->
102	# internal_error 500; PLAN 3.5 binds it to 409 / "audit.append_only" (an append-only
103	# write is a client-visible conflict, not an opaque server fault), so this map follows
104	# the task. Finance tokens below are pre-registered for PLAN 4 and keep D-014's codes.
105	DB_GUARD_TOKEN_MAP: dict[str, tuple[int, str]] = {
106	    "ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY": (409, "audit.append_only"),
107	    "ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED": (422, "finance.period_closed"),
108	    "ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE": (422, "finance.entry_immutable"),
109	    "ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY": (422, "finance.journal_unbalanced"),
110	}
111	
112	
113	def translate_db_guard_error(exc: DBAPIError) -> AtlasError | None:
114	    """Map a trigger-raised ATLAS_* token in a DBAPIError to an AtlasError, or None if the
115	    error carries no known token (then it is a genuine integrity/operational failure and
116	    the catch-all 500 handler owns it). Matching is on the full message text because the
117	    token is embedded in the raised exception string on both engines."""
118	    message = str(exc.orig) if exc.orig is not None else str(exc)
119	    for token, (status_code, code) in DB_GUARD_TOKEN_MAP.items():
120	        if token in message:
121	            return AtlasError(code=code, message=token, status_code=status_code)
122	    return None

1	"""Conditional GETs on slow-changing reference data — collection-level weak ETags (D-035).
2	
3	PERFORMANCE §3 requires ``ETag/If-None-Match`` on slow-changing reference collections (chart of
4	accounts, currencies, tax codes, fiscal calendar, posting defaults). This is a justified core
5	flat file (the same precedent as core/pagination.py): the validator machinery is cross-cutting,
6	mentions no business concept, and every reference endpoint composes it the same way.
7	
8	**Why collection-level, not row-level.** A row-level ETag would validate one entity; a list
9	endpoint returns a *page* of a collection, and the cheapest correct validator for "has anything in
10	this collection changed?" is a single aggregate ``SELECT COUNT(id), MAX(updated_at)`` over the
11	tenant's rows. Any insert moves the count; any update moves ``MAX(updated_at)`` (TimestampMixin's
12	``onupdate``); a delete moves the count (and usually the max). So the pair ``(count, max_updated)``
13	is a sound WEAK validator for the whole collection. The cost: any change to the collection
14	invalidates *every* page's cached validator — acceptable for small reference sets, which is exactly
15	the data this is applied to (PERFORMANCE §3 scopes it to reference data only, never transactional
16	lists). Deletes that leave count unchanged are impossible for a pure delete; a delete-then-insert
17	in the same instant could in principle pin both count and max, so we additionally guard correctness
18	with the request fingerprint below — but for the data this covers the (count, max) pair is the
19	dominant signal.
20	
21	**Tenant component (D-007).** The aggregate select references the model's columns
22	(``func.count(model.id)``), so the ``do_orm_execute`` tenancy listener engages and scopes the
23	COUNT/MAX to the current tenant automatically (verified: a ``func`` aggregate over mapped columns
24	carries the mapper, so ``all_mappers`` detects it). The tenant id is *also* baked into the ETag
25	string as a short component, so even if two tenants happened to hold the same (count, max) the
26	validators differ — a cross-tenant 304 is impossible by construction, belt-and-suspenders over the
27	already tenant-scoped aggregate.
28	
29	**Request fingerprint (the key correctness point).** The ETag represents the *whole collection's*
30	version, not one page. A naive collection-level validator would let a client that cached page 2
31	receive a 304 for a request for page 5 (same collection, unchanged) and then render the wrong
32	slice. To prevent that, the request's cursor + limit + filters are hashed into the ETag, so the
33	validator is unique per (collection-version, page-request). A 304 can therefore only ever be served
34	for the *identical* page request whose body the client already holds.
35	
36	**Format.** ``W/"<count>-<max_updated_at_micros>-<tenant8>-<reqfingerprint>"`` — a weak validator
37	(``W/`` prefix) because two byte-different but semantically-equal page renderings (e.g. ordering
38	ties) should still match. Empty collection → ``W/"0--<tenant8>-<reqfingerprint>"`` (a stable
39	``max`` component of empty string), which still changes the moment the first row is inserted.
40	"""
41	
42	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
43	
44	import sqlalchemy as sa
45	from fastapi import Request, Response
46	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
47	
48	from app.core.tenancy import get_current_tenant_id
49	
50	# 304 carries no body; only the validator header rides back so the client can revalidate again.
51	NOT_MODIFIED_STATUS = 304
52	
53	
54	def _tenant_component() -> str:
55	    """Short, stable tenant marker for the ETag. The aggregate is already tenant-scoped by the
56	    D-007 listener; this makes a cross-tenant validator collision impossible even in theory, since
57	    two tenants' validators differ in this component regardless of their (count, max). Reads the
58	    request's tenant from the ContextVar (set by core/deps.get_current_user)."""
59	    tenant_id = get_current_tenant_id()
60	    # get_current_tenant_id is fail-closed and only returns None under system_context, which a
61	    # tenant reference endpoint never runs under; guard anyway so the helper is total.
62	    return tenant_id.hex[:8] if tenant_id is not None else "system"
63	
64	
65	async def collection_etag(
66	    session: AsyncSession,
67	    model: type,
68	    *extra_filters: sa.ColumnElement[bool],
69	    request_fingerprint: str = "",
70	) -> str:
71	    """Compute a WEAK collection validator from ONE cheap aggregate query (D-035).
72	
73	    ``SELECT COUNT(model.id), MAX(model.updated_at)`` — tenant-scoped automatically by the D-007
74	    ``do_orm_execute`` listener (the aggregate references the model's mapped columns, so the
75	    tenant predicate is injected). ``extra_filters`` narrow the collection to the same rows the
76	    list endpoint returns (e.g. a ``fiscal_year_id`` filter), so the validator tracks the visible
77	    slice, not the whole table. ``request_fingerprint`` (cursor+limit+filters of the actual
78	    request) is folded into the returned tag so a 304 can never serve a different page slice.
79	
80	    The returned string is the full weak ETag ready for the ``ETag`` header / ``If-None-Match``
81	    comparison: ``W/"<count>-<max_micros>-<tenant8>-<reqfingerprint>"``.
82	    """
83	    stmt = sa.select(sa.func.count(model.id), sa.func.max(model.updated_at))
84	    for clause in extra_filters:
85	        stmt = stmt.where(clause)
86	    count, max_updated = (await session.execute(stmt)).one()
87	
88	    # Microsecond epoch keeps the component compact and monotonic; empty collection → "" so the
89	    # validator is stable for an empty set yet flips the moment the first row lands (count 0->1).
90	    max_component = (
91	        "" if max_updated is None else str(int(max_updated.timestamp() * 1_000_000))
92	    )
93	    return f'W/"{count}-{max_component}-{_tenant_component()}-{request_fingerprint}"'
94	
95	
96	def _normalize_tag(raw: str) -> str:
97	    """Strip a leading weak marker so weak/strong forms of the same tag compare equal. Per RFC
98	    7232 the weak-comparison function ignores the ``W/`` prefix; our validators are always weak,
99	    but a client may echo the value with or without it, so normalize both sides."""
100	    raw = raw.strip()
101	    if raw.startswith("W/"):
102	        raw = raw[2:]
103	    return raw
104	
105	
106	def check_not_modified(request: Request, etag: str) -> bool:
107	    """True when the client's ``If-None-Match`` satisfies ``etag`` (RFC 7232 weak comparison).
108	
109	    Handles the ``*`` value (matches any existing representation → 304 whenever the resource
110	    exists) and a comma-separated list of candidate tags. Comparison is weak: the ``W/`` prefix is
111	    ignored on both sides. A missing/blank header → False (the endpoint then serves a normal 200).
112	    """
113	    header = request.headers.get("if-none-match")
114	    if not header:
115	        return False
116	    candidates = [part.strip() for part in header.split(",") if part.strip()]
117	    if "*" in candidates:
118	        return True
119	    target = _normalize_tag(etag)
120	    return any(_normalize_tag(candidate) == target for candidate in candidates)
121	
122	
123	async def conditional_response[T](
124	    request: Request,
125	    response: Response,
126	    etag: str,
127	    builder: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]],
128	) -> T | Response:
129	    """Conditional-GET epilogue for a reference list endpoint (D-035).
130	
131	    Given the already-computed collection ``etag``: if the client's ``If-None-Match`` matches,
132	    return a bare ``304`` carrying ONLY the ``ETag`` header and NO body — and crucially WITHOUT
133	    awaiting ``builder``, so the expensive full-page query never runs on the 304 path (this is what
134	    makes a conditional request cheaper than the unconditional one). Otherwise set the ``ETag``
135	    header on the real response and return ``await builder()`` (the ``Page`` payload).
136	
137	    Returning a starlette ``Response`` directly bypasses the route's ``response_model``, so FastAPI
138	    does not try to validate the empty 304 body against ``Page[T]`` (verified by a test).
139	    """
140	    if check_not_modified(request, etag):
141	        return Response(status_code=NOT_MODIFIED_STATUS, headers={"ETag": etag})
142	    response.headers["ETag"] = etag
143	    return await builder()
144	
145	
146	def request_fingerprint(cursor: str | None, limit: int, *filter_parts: object) -> str:
147	    """Stable per-request fingerprint folded into the collection ETag so a 304 can only ever be
148	    served for the IDENTICAL page request (D-035). Reuses the pagination filter-fingerprint hash so
149	    the cursor/limit/filter identity matches what ``paginate`` already keys cursors on — one source
150	    of truth for "which slice of the collection is this request asking for"."""
151	    # Imported lazily: core/pagination imports core/schemas which is heavy; keeping the import here
152	    # avoids any import-order coupling and this helper is called per request, not at module load.
153	    from app.core.pagination import filter_fingerprint
154	
155	    return filter_fingerprint(cursor, limit, *filter_parts)
156	
157	
158	__all__ = [
159	    "check_not_modified",
160	    "collection_etag",
161	    "conditional_response",
162	    "request_fingerprint",
163	]

1	"""D-011 domain-event bus: collect-then-dispatch, in the SAME transaction.
2	
3	Three pieces, exactly as D-011 prescribes:
4	
5	* ``DomainEvent`` — a frozen Pydantic v2 base. Each subclass declares a ClassVar
6	  ``key`` (module-prefixed past-tense string, e.g. ``'sales.order.shipped'``) and
7	  carries ``tenant_id`` + ``occurred_at`` plus its own payload fields. Events are
8	  PLAIN DATA — no behaviour — so a publishing module's ``events.py`` is a sanctioned
9	  cross-module import (STRUCTURE §5 amendment, D-011): a subscriber in another module's
10	  ``handlers.py`` imports the typed event class without importing any logic.
11	
12	* The subscription registry — ``subscribe(key, handler)`` and the ``@on(EventClass)``
13	  decorator a module's ``handlers.py`` calls at import time; ``clear_subscriptions()``
14	  / ``subscriptions_snapshot()`` / ``restore_subscriptions()`` give the tests a clean
15	  registry per case so module-registered handlers in later phases never leak.
16	
17	* ``InProcessEventBus`` behind the ``EventBus`` Protocol, plus the single shared
18	  unit-of-work drain point ``run_in_uow``:
19	  - ``publish(session, event)`` appends to a FIFO buffer in ``session.info`` — NO
20	    immediate dispatch, so handlers observe the publisher's settled aggregate state.
21	  - ``run_in_uow(session, work)`` runs the business ``work``, then drains the buffer
22	    breadth-first (FIFO), invoking each handler with the SAME session so its writes
23	    land in the SAME transaction, THEN commits. A handler may publish further events;
24	    those are drained too, up to ``MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW`` total, then ``EventCycleError``.
25	    ANY exception — business work or any handler — rolls the whole transaction back and
26	    re-raises: deliberately NO per-handler isolation (if the COGS posting fails, the
27	    goods issue must not commit). This is the load-bearing all-or-nothing invariant.
28	
29	**Handler order** is deterministic: per event key, handlers fire in registration order
30	(module import order in main.py's app factory); events fire in publish (FIFO) order.
31	
32	**Tenant context** (D-007): handlers run UNDER the trigger's already-active tenant
33	context, so their tenant-scoped reads/writes are filtered and stamped like any other
34	write. A handler doing system-level work wraps it in ``system_context()`` itself (the
35	D-007 site-4 "bus system-event replay" seam) — the bus does not change context for it.
36	
37	**Audit** (D-010): handler writes share the session, so the before_flush/after_flush
38	audit listeners capture and tenant-stamp them automatically — no extra wiring (proven
39	by tests/core/test_events.py).
40	
41	**Swap path:** the in-transaction semantics ARE the contract, expressed by the
42	``EventBus`` Protocol. A future ``TransactionalOutboxBus`` implements the same Protocol,
43	writing ``core_event_outbox`` rows in the same transaction for an external relay, with
44	zero business-logic changes. The outbox TABLE is introduced THEN (a later PLAN task),
45	not now — v1 ships only the in-process bus.
46	"""
47	
48	import uuid
49	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
50	from datetime import UTC, datetime
51	from typing import ClassVar, Protocol, runtime_checkable
52	
53	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
54	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
55	
56	from app.core.exceptions import AtlasError
57	
58	# Hard ceiling on handler dispatches per unit of work (D-011): handlers may publish
59	# further events, drained in the same uow, but a cycle (A -> B -> A) or a runaway fan-out
60	# would otherwise hold the transaction open forever. At the cap we raise rather than spin.
61	MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW = 50
62	
63	# FIFO buffer of not-yet-dispatched events, keyed in session.info so it is per-session
64	# (per-transaction) and never shared across requests.
65	_BUFFER_KEY = "pending_events"
66	
67	
68	class EventCycleError(AtlasError):
69	    """A unit of work dispatched more than MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW events — almost always
70	    a handler-publish cycle. Surfaced as a 500 (a server-side wiring fault, not client
71	    input) and, like every handler failure, rolls the whole transaction back (D-011)."""
72	
73	    def __init__(self, dispatched: int) -> None:
74	        super().__init__(
75	            code="events.cycle_detected",
76	            message=(
77	                f"Event dispatch exceeded the per-transaction cap of "
78	                f"{MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW} (dispatched {dispatched}); likely a handler "
79	                "publish cycle."
80	            ),
81	            status_code=500,
82	        )
83	
84	
85	class DomainEvent(BaseModel):
86	    """Base for every domain event (D-011). Frozen + plain data, no behaviour.
87	
88	    Subclasses declare their string key and payload:
89	
90	        class SalesOrderShipped(DomainEvent):
91	            key: ClassVar[str] = "sales.order.shipped"
92	            order_id: uuid.UUID
93	
94	    ``key`` is a ClassVar (one value per event TYPE, not a per-instance field) so it is
95	    not part of the payload schema; ``tenant_id`` + ``occurred_at`` are carried on every
96	    event. ``frozen=True`` makes instances immutable — an event is a fact that happened.
97	    """
98	
99	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
100	
101	    # Declared on the base as a sentinel; every concrete subclass overrides it. Kept as a
102	    # ClassVar so Pydantic does not treat it as a payload field.
103	    key: ClassVar[str] = ""
104	
105	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID
106	    occurred_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(UTC))
107	
108	
109	# A handler is an async callable taking the shared session and the event, returning None.
110	# It runs before commit, inside the trigger's transaction and tenant context (D-011/D-007).
111	Handler = Callable[[AsyncSession, DomainEvent], Awaitable[None]]
112	
113	# Registry: event key -> handlers in registration order. Module import order (main.py's
114	# app factory) therefore fixes handler order deterministically (D-011).
115	_subscriptions: dict[str, list[Handler]] = {}
116	
117	
118	def subscribe(event_key: str, handler: Handler) -> None:
119	    """Register ``handler`` for ``event_key``. Called by a module's handlers.py at import,
120	    directly or via the ``@on`` decorator. Order of registration = dispatch order."""
121	    _subscriptions.setdefault(event_key, []).append(handler)
122	
123	
124	def on(event_type: type[DomainEvent]) -> Callable[[Handler], Handler]:
125	    """Decorator form of subscribe, keyed off the event CLASS so handlers.py stays typed:
126	
127	        @on(SalesOrderShipped)
128	        async def post_cogs(session: AsyncSession, event: SalesOrderShipped) -> None: ...
129	
130	    Returns the handler unchanged so it can still be called/tested directly."""
131	
132	    def decorator(handler: Handler) -> Handler:
133	        subscribe(event_type.key, handler)
134	        return handler
135	
136	    return decorator
137	
138	
139	def handlers_for(event_key: str) -> tuple[Handler, ...]:
140	    """Registered handlers for a key, in registration order (empty tuple if none)."""
141	    return tuple(_subscriptions.get(event_key, ()))
142	
143	
144	def clear_subscriptions() -> None:
145	    """Drop every registration. The autouse test fixture calls this so handlers a module
146	    registers at import in later phases cannot leak between tests (D-025 isolation)."""
147	    _subscriptions.clear()
148	
149	
150	def subscriptions_snapshot() -> dict[str, list[Handler]]:
151	    """Deep-ish copy of the registry for save/restore around a test that mutates it."""
152	    return {key: list(value) for key, value in _subscriptions.items()}
153	
154	
155	def restore_subscriptions(snapshot: dict[str, list[Handler]]) -> None:
156	    """Replace the registry with a previously taken snapshot."""
157	    _subscriptions.clear()
158	    _subscriptions.update({key: list(value) for key, value in snapshot.items()})
159	
160	
161	def _buffer(session: AsyncSession) -> list[DomainEvent]:
162	    return session.info.setdefault(_BUFFER_KEY, [])
163	
164	
165	@runtime_checkable
166	class EventBus(Protocol):
167	    """The swappable contract (D-011). The in-transaction semantics live in ``run_in_uow``,
168	    not here, so any implementation (in-process now, a transactional-outbox bus later)
169	    publishes the same way and business logic never changes. ``publish`` buffers; it does
170	    NOT dispatch — dispatch is owned by the single ``run_in_uow`` drain point."""
171	
172	    def publish(self, session: AsyncSession, event: DomainEvent) -> None: ...
173	
174	
175	class InProcessEventBus:
176	    """The only EventBus implementation in v1 (D-011). ``publish`` appends to the per-session
177	    FIFO buffer; the buffer is drained by ``run_in_uow`` after the business work and before
178	    commit, so handlers run synchronously in the trigger's transaction."""
179	
180	    def publish(self, session: AsyncSession, event: DomainEvent) -> None:
181	        _buffer(session).append(event)
182	
183	
184	# Module-level singleton: services import this and call ``bus.publish(session, event)``.
185	# A later outbox bus replaces THIS binding (same Protocol) and nothing else moves.
186	bus: EventBus = InProcessEventBus()
187	
188	
189	def publish(session: AsyncSession, event: DomainEvent) -> None:
190	    """Convenience free function delegating to the active bus, so callers can
191	    ``from app.core.events import publish`` without reaching for the singleton."""
192	    bus.publish(session, event)
193	
194	
195	async def _drain_and_dispatch(session: AsyncSession) -> None:
196	    """Pop buffered events FIFO and run their handlers, sharing ``session``. Handlers may
197	    publish more events (appended to the same buffer); we keep draining breadth-first up to
198	    MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW total dispatches, then raise EventCycleError. A handler raising
199	    propagates — run_in_uow's caller rolls the whole transaction back (D-011: no isolation).
200	    """
201	    buffer = _buffer(session)
202	    dispatched = 0
203	    while buffer:
204	        event = buffer.pop(0)  # FIFO: oldest first
205	        for handler in handlers_for(event.key):
206	            if dispatched >= MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW:
207	                raise EventCycleError(dispatched)
208	            await handler(session, event)
209	            dispatched += 1
210	    # Defensive: an event with no handler still counts toward nothing; a cap breach can
211	    # only happen above. Clearing the (now empty) key keeps session.info tidy.
212	    session.info.pop(_BUFFER_KEY, None)
213	
214	
215	async def run_in_uow(
216	    session: AsyncSession,
217	    work: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]] | Awaitable[None],
218	) -> None:
219	    """The single sanctioned unit-of-work helper (D-011). Used by the request session
220	    dependency (core/deps), by seed.py and by CLI flows, so HTTP, seed and tests get
221	    IDENTICAL event semantics.
222	
223	    Sequence: run ``work`` (the business mutation that publishes events) -> drain the
224	    buffered events FIFO and run their handlers on the SAME session (so handler effects,
225	    e.g. a COGS journal, are in the same transaction as the trigger, e.g. the stock
226	    issue) -> commit. If the business work OR any handler raises (or the cascade cap is
227	    hit), roll the WHOLE transaction back and re-raise — the trigger's own writes do not
228	    persist. Handlers run under the trigger's active tenant context (D-007); nothing here
229	    changes it.
230	
231	    ``work`` may be a coroutine object or a zero-arg callable returning an awaitable, so
232	    both ``run_in_uow(session, service_coro)`` and ``run_in_uow(session, lambda: ...)``
233	    read naturally at call sites.
234	    """
235	    try:
236	        awaitable = work() if callable(work) else work
237	        await awaitable
238	        await _drain_and_dispatch(session)
239	        await session.commit()
240	    except Exception:
241	        await session.rollback()
242	        # Drop any partially drained / leftover buffer so the next uow on this session
243	        # (tests reuse one session) starts clean.
244	        session.info.pop(_BUFFER_KEY, None)
245	        raise
246

1	"""Sales document types, number sequences, docflow link types and domain-event keys (D-012/D-040).
2	
3	Split out of the single ``constants.py`` at the 400-line cap (PLAN 7.4). Each sales document
4	(quote, order, delivery, billing, return) registers in core_documents and claims a gapless number AT
5	CREATION (D-040, the procurement-document precedent — not finance's number-at-post branch). The

13	# claim-at-creation so a quote/order is referenceable the moment it exists — the
14	# procurement-document

20	QUOTE_NUMBER_PADDING = 5

28	# the

30	# the order raised from it (the order carries source_quote_id; the quote→order edge is the chain the
31	# DocFlowViewer renders). The reverse ("quoted_by") is the successor's view, kept here for the docs.
32	QUOTE_CONVERTED_TO_ORDER_LINK = "converted_to"
33	
34	# Delivery (PLAN 7.3): the outbound fulfilment document. Registers in core_documents + claims a
35	# gapless DN number AT CREATION (D-040; year-resetting DN-2026-00001), the goods-receipt precedent.
36	# A delivery is built DRAFT then POSTED; the POST issues stock (an inventory ISSUE move per line)

40	DELIVERY_SEQUENCE_NAME = "sales.delivery"
41	DELIVERY_NUMBER_PREFIX = "DN"
42	DELIVERY_NUMBER_PADDING = 5

44	# Delivery docflow edges (PLAN 7.3, D-041). The edge is predecessor → successor named from the
45	# predecessor's point of view:
46	#   order → delivery   : the sales order is "delivered_by" the delivery (written by sales at POST).
47	#   delivery → move    : the delivery is "moved_by" each inventory ISSUE move it generates (written
48	#                        by INVENTORY's handler when it creates the moves — the GR "moved_by"
49	#                        precedent; the delivery↔move linkage is docflow, NOT a cross-module FK).
50	ORDER_DELIVERED_BY_DELIVERY_LINK = "delivered_by"
51	DELIVERY_MOVED_BY_STOCK_MOVE_LINK = "moved_by"
52	
53	# The sales domain event the delivery POST publishes (D-011/D-041): inventory's handlers.py
54	# subscribes and creates the stock ISSUE moves in the SAME transaction (the sanctioned cross-module
55	# mechanism — sales never imports inventory/service). Mirrors GOODS_RECEIPT_POSTED_EVENT_KEY, but
56	# the event carries NO GL accounts: an ISSUE move's default offset IS the item-category COGS

58	# override.
59	DELIVERY_SHIPPED_EVENT_KEY = "sales.delivery.shipped"
60	
61	
62	# --- Billing (PLAN 7.4, D-046) ------------------------------------------------
63	# The sales-side billing document. Registers in core_documents + claims a gapless BIL number AT
64	# CREATION (D-040; year-resetting BIL-2026-00001), the delivery precedent. A billing is built DRAFT
65	# then POSTED; the POST publishes the billing event so FINANCE creates + posts the AR customer
66	# invoice (Dr AR / Cr revenue + tax) — but the billing claims its OWN BIL- number, distinct from the
67	# INV- the finance customer invoice claims (D-046: two numbers, the sales doc triggers the finance
68	# doc, mirroring the procurement match → AP bill split).
69	BILLING_DOC_TYPE = "sales.billing"
70	BILLING_SEQUENCE_NAME = "sales.billing"
71	BILLING_NUMBER_PREFIX = "BIL"
72	BILLING_NUMBER_PADDING = 5

74	# Billing docflow edges (PLAN 7.4, D-046). Each edge is predecessor → successor, named from the
75	# predecessor's point of view:
76	#   order    → billing : the sales order is "billed_by" the billing (written by sales at POST).
77	# delivery → billing : each delivery a billing bills is "invoiced_by" the billing (written by sales
78	#                        at create from the lines' delivery_line_id).
79	#   billing  → invoice : the billing is "invoiced_by_invoice" the FINANCE customer invoice it
80	#                        triggers (written by FINANCE's handler when it posts the AR invoice — the
81	# match→bill 'billed_by' precedent; the billing↔invoice link is docflow, NOT a
82	#                        cross-module FK).

84	DELIVERY_INVOICED_BY_BILLING_LINK = "invoiced_by"
85	BILLING_INVOICED_BY_INVOICE_LINK = "invoiced_by_invoice"

89	# mechanism — sales never imports finance/service). The MIRROR of procurement's

91	# (match → AP bill), sign-flipped to billing → AR invoice. The event carries the resolved AR control
92	# + sales-revenue accounts (sales reads them from finance/queries before publishing) so the handler
93	# is a thin builder, exactly like the AP-bill handler.
94	BILLING_POSTED_EVENT_KEY = "sales.billing.posted"
95	
96	
97	# --- Returns / RMA (PLAN 7.4, D-046) ------------------------------------------
98	# The reverse-O2C document. Registers in core_documents + claims a gapless RMA number AT CREATION
99	# (D-040; year-resetting RMA-2026-00001). A return is built DRAFT then POSTED; the POST publishes
100	# TWO
101	# events: one the inventory handler turns into a stock RECEIPT move (goods back, Dr Inventory / Cr
102	# COGS — the COGS-offset OVERRIDE reverses the issue) and one the finance handler turns into an AR
103	# credit note (Dr revenue / Cr AR — reversing the billing). The return claims its OWN RMA- number,
104	# distinct from the STK- the inventory move and the CN- the finance credit note claim.
105	RETURN_DOC_TYPE = "sales.return"
106	RETURN_SEQUENCE_NAME = "sales.return"
107	RETURN_NUMBER_PREFIX = "RMA"
108	RETURN_NUMBER_PADDING = 5
109	
110	# Return docflow edges (PLAN 7.4, D-046). Each edge predecessor → successor from the predecessor's
111	# view:
112	#   order   → return      : the sales order is "returned_by" the return (written by sales at POST).
113	#   return  → stock-move   : the return is "received_by" each inventory RECEIPT move it generates
114	#                            (written by INVENTORY's handler when it creates the moves — the
115	#                            delivery 'moved_by' precedent; the return↔move link is docflow, NOT a
116	#                            cross-module FK).
117	# return  → credit-note  : the return is "credited_by" the FINANCE credit note it triggers (written
118	#                            by FINANCE's handler when it posts the credit note).
119	ORDER_RETURNED_BY_RETURN_LINK = "returned_by"
120	RETURN_RECEIVED_BY_STOCK_MOVE_LINK = "received_by"
121	RETURN_CREDITED_BY_CREDIT_NOTE_LINK = "credited_by"

2

5	imports only finance/queries downward. Keep this surface thin and stable — it is a contract; it is
6	the ONLY inventory file other modules import.
7

9	item's base UoM and costing method, and the category's GL-account wiring (so the COGS handler can
10	resolve where to post when stock issues land in 5.2+). PLAN 5.2 adds the ON-HAND projection reads
11	(``total_on_hand``, ``on_hand_by_bin``, ``on_hand_by_lot``) — what sales ATP and procurement will
12	call: they read the MAINTAINED ``inv_stock_quants`` projection (D-036), an indexed aggregate, never
13	an unbounded SUM over the move history (PERFORMANCE §1).
14	
15	Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under the caller's tenant context, so the
16	D-007 filter applies on top of the explicit predicate — ordinary tenant-scoped reads, not a bypass.
17	"""
18	
19	import uuid
20	from decimal import Decimal
21	
22	from sqlalchemy import func, select

40	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
41	) -> Item | None:
42	    """The item with ``item_id`` in the tenant, or None. Lets another module read an item's master
43	    fields (name, type, base UoM, costing method) without importing inventory models directly."""
44	    stmt = select(Item).where(Item.tenant_id == tenant_id, Item.id == item_id)
45	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()

50	) -> bool:

52	    procurement line uses to validate its item_id dimension (the inventory analogue of finance's
53	    ``account_exists_by_id``)."""
54	    stmt = select(Item.id).where(Item.tenant_id == tenant_id, Item.id == item_id)
55	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None

59	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, uom_id: uuid.UUID
60	) -> bool:

62	    ``item_exists``: a manufacturing BOM header/component references the parent/component UoM by
63	    opaque id (D-029) and validates it through this contract before writing — UoMs and items are

1	"""D-015 exact money/quantity/rate representation on BOTH engines, plus allocation.
2	
3	The financial engine's DB-level invariants (the balance trigger, the one-side CHECK,
4	valuation math) are only meaningful if storage is EXACT on both backends. PostgreSQL has a
5	native NUMERIC; SQLite does not — ``sa.Numeric`` round-trips through float there and silently
6	loses precision. So each TypeDecorator stores NUMERIC on Postgres and an INTEGER of scaled
7	minor units on SQLite (value × 10^scale), converting to/from ``decimal.Decimal`` in the bind/
8	result processors. Trigger SQL therefore only ever SUMs and COMPARES the stored representation
9	(ints on SQLite, NUMERIC on PG) — never divides or scales — so the asymmetric storage stays
10	semantically identical where it matters (D-015 trigger discipline).
11	
12	Scales:
13	- ``MoneyType``      NUMERIC(18,6) / INTEGER micro-units (×10^6), scale 6 — headroom over the
14	  2/3 currency decimals so posting-time rounding has somewhere to live.
15	- ``QuantityType``   NUMERIC(18,6) / INTEGER micro-units (×10^6), scale 6 — UoM/FIFO math.
16	- ``RateType``       NUMERIC(20,10) / INTEGER nano-units (×10^10), scale 10 — FX rates keep
17	  full precision (rates are never quantized to currency decimals).
18	
19	Python is Decimal-only — never float. The TypeDecorators are ``cache_ok = True`` (they carry
20	no per-instance state beyond the fixed class scale), so SQLAlchemy may cache compiled
21	statements that use them.
22	
23	``allocate`` is the single largest-remainder splitter (D-015): tax/discount splits, payment
24	allocation, and the journal's functional-currency residual-cent balancing all route through it
25	so parts always sum EXACTLY to the total. ``quantize_money`` is the ROUND_HALF_UP boundary
26	rounding (commercial/SAP practice), keyed off a per-currency decimal-places lookup.
27	"""
28	
29	from __future__ import annotations
30	
31	from decimal import ROUND_DOWN, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
32	
33	import sqlalchemy as sa
34	from sqlalchemy.engine import Dialect
35	from sqlalchemy.types import TypeDecorator
36	
37	# Scales (number of fractional decimal digits each type stores).
38	_MONEY_SCALE = 6
39	_QUANTITY_SCALE = 6
40	_RATE_SCALE = 10
41	
42	
43	class _ScaledDecimalType(TypeDecorator[Decimal]):
44	    """Shared base for the three exact-decimal types (D-015).
45	
46	    ``impl`` is NUMERIC so the default (Postgres) rendering is a true decimal; on SQLite the
47	    column is loaded as INTEGER and the bind/result processors translate Decimal <-> scaled
48	    integer minor units. The conversion is exact in both directions because a Decimal with at
49	    most ``scale`` fractional digits maps to an integer with no rounding (values carrying more
50	    digits than the scale are quantized HALF_UP on the way in — money/quantities are quantized
51	    at their boundary before storage, so this only ever trims trailing noise)."""
52	
53	    # Required by TypeDecorator: the default (Postgres) decorated type. ``load_dialect_impl``
54	    # overrides it per dialect (BigInteger on SQLite, Numeric(precision, scale) on PG).
55	    impl = sa.Numeric
56	    cache_ok = True
57	
58	    # Concrete subclasses set these; the base is abstract by virtue of unset class attrs.
59	    scale: int
60	    precision: int
61	
62	    @property
63	    def python_type(self) -> type[Decimal]:
64	        return Decimal
65	
66	    def load_dialect_impl(self, dialect: Dialect) -> sa.types.TypeEngine[object]:
67	        if dialect.name == "sqlite":
68	            # Scaled minor units fit a 64-bit integer for the demo/test value ranges (D-015).
69	            return dialect.type_descriptor(sa.BigInteger())
70	        return dialect.type_descriptor(sa.Numeric(self.precision, self.scale))
71	
72	    @property
73	    def _quantum(self) -> Decimal:
74	        return Decimal(1).scaleb(-self.scale)
75	
76	    def process_bind_param(self, value: Decimal | int | str | None, dialect: Dialect):
77	        if value is None:
78	            return None
79	        as_decimal = value if isinstance(value, Decimal) else Decimal(str(value))
80	        if dialect.name == "sqlite":
81	            # Decimal -> integer scaled minor units. Quantize first so a value with more than
82	            # ``scale`` digits cannot leave a fractional remainder when multiplied out.
83	            scaled = as_decimal.quantize(self._quantum, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
84	            return int(scaled.scaleb(self.scale))
85	        return as_decimal
86	
87	    def process_result_value(self, value: int | Decimal | None, dialect: Dialect) -> Decimal | None:
88	        if value is None:
89	            return None
90	        if dialect.name == "sqlite":
91	            # Integer scaled minor units -> Decimal at the type's scale (exact, no float).
92	            return (Decimal(int(value)) * self._quantum).quantize(self._quantum)
93	        return value if isinstance(value, Decimal) else Decimal(str(value))
94	
95	
96	class MoneyType(_ScaledDecimalType):
97	    """Monetary amount (D-015): NUMERIC(18,6) on Postgres, INTEGER micro-units on SQLite."""
98	
99	    # cache_ok must be set on each concrete TypeDecorator class, not just the base.
100	    cache_ok = True
101	    scale = _MONEY_SCALE
102	    precision = 18
103	
104	
105	class QuantityType(_ScaledDecimalType):
106	    """Inventory quantity (D-015): NUMERIC(18,6) on Postgres, INTEGER micro-units on SQLite.
107	    Same storage as MoneyType but a distinct type so quantity and money columns read clearly."""
108	
109	    cache_ok = True
110	    scale = _QUANTITY_SCALE
111	    precision = 18
112	
113	
114	class RateType(_ScaledDecimalType):
115	    """FX/exchange rate (D-015): NUMERIC(20,10) on Postgres, INTEGER nano-units on SQLite.
116	    Scale 10 keeps full rate precision — rates are never quantized to currency decimals."""
117	
118	    cache_ok = True
119	    scale = _RATE_SCALE
120	    precision = 20
121	
122	
123	# --- Currency decimals + boundary rounding ------------------------------------
124	
125	# ISO 4217 fractional digits. Default is 2; non-2-decimal currencies are listed explicitly so
126	# the table can grow (JPY=0, BHD=3, ...). Stored journal amounts quantize to this at the
127	# posting/pricing boundary; unit prices/costs and FX rates keep full scale-6/10 precision.
128	_DEFAULT_CURRENCY_DECIMALS = 2
129	_CURRENCY_DECIMALS: dict[str, int] = {
130	    "JPY": 0,
131	    "KRW": 0,
132	    "BHD": 3,
133	    "KWD": 3,
134	    "OMR": 3,
135	    "TND": 3,
136	}
137	
138	
139	def currency_decimals(currency_code: str) -> int:
140	    """ISO 4217 fractional digits for ``currency_code`` (default 2). The amount-rounding
141	    boundary uses this so e.g. JPY rounds to whole units and BHD to three places (D-015)."""
142	    return _CURRENCY_DECIMALS.get(currency_code.upper(), _DEFAULT_CURRENCY_DECIMALS)
143	
144	
145	def quantize_money(value: Decimal, places: int = 2) -> Decimal:
146	    """Round ``value`` to ``places`` decimals HALF_UP (D-015 — commercial/SAP practice). Pass
147	    ``currency_decimals(code)`` for ``places`` to round to a currency's minor unit."""
148	    return value.quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-places), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
149	
150	
151	def quantize_for_currency(value: Decimal, currency_code: str) -> Decimal:
152	    """Round ``value`` to ``currency_code``'s minor unit HALF_UP (D-015)."""
153	    return quantize_money(value, currency_decimals(currency_code))
154	
155	
156	def allocate(total: Decimal, weights: list[Decimal], places: int = 2) -> list[Decimal]:
157	    """Split ``total`` across ``weights`` so the parts sum EXACTLY to ``total`` (D-015).
158	
159	    Largest-remainder method: each part is ``total × weight / Σweights`` rounded DOWN to
160	    ``places`` decimals, then the rounding residual (``total`` minus the sum of floored parts)
161	    is distributed one minor unit at a time to the parts with the largest fractional remainder,
162	    ties broken by original index. Deterministic, and the parts ALWAYS reconstitute the total —
163	    used for FX residual-cent absorption, tax splits, discount splits and payment allocation.
164	
165	    A zero or empty total returns zeros; zero total weight (all weights zero) splits ``total``
166	    evenly via equal unit weights so the result still sums to ``total`` rather than dropping it.
167	    """
168	    quantum = Decimal(1).scaleb(-places)
169	    n = len(weights)
170	    if n == 0:
171	        return []
172	    total_weight = sum(weights, Decimal(0))
173	    if total_weight == 0:
174	        # Degenerate: no weight to distribute by. Fall back to equal weights so the total is
175	        # still allocated exactly (never silently dropped).
176	        weights = [Decimal(1)] * n
177	        total_weight = Decimal(n)
178	
179	    exact = [total * weight / total_weight for weight in weights]
180	    floored = [part.quantize(quantum, rounding=ROUND_DOWN) for part in exact]
181	    remainders = [exact[i] - floored[i] for i in range(n)]
182	
183	    allocated = sum(floored, Decimal(0))
184	    residual = total - allocated
185	    # Number of whole minor units still to hand out (can be negative if total is negative).
186	    units = int((residual / quantum).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
187	
188	    # Distribute to the largest remainders first; for a negative residual hand out negative
189	    # units to the SMALLEST remainders (those rounded least-down) so the result stays balanced.
190	    order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: (remainders[i], -i), reverse=units >= 0)
191	    step = quantum if units >= 0 else -quantum
192	    for k in range(abs(units)):
193	        floored[order[k % n]] += step
194	    return floored
195	
196	
197	__all__ = [
198	    "MoneyType",
199	    "QuantityType",
200	    "RateType",
201	    "allocate",
202	    "currency_decimals",
203	    "quantize_for_currency",
204	    "quantize_money",

"""CRM module (PLAN 12.1, the SINGLE Phase 12 plan) — the CRM-lite pre-sales pipeline.

PLAN 12.1 delivers the deliberately small CRM core (s4hana-parity §CRM/Sales-pipeline scope): LEADS
that QUALIFY and CONVERT into OPPORTUNITIES, an opportunity KANBAN whose STAGE is the column (moving a
card = moving the stage), ACTIVITIES (calls/emails/meetings/tasks/notes) logged against a lead OR an
opportunity, and the headline CONVERT-TO-CUSTOMER+QUOTE that turns a won opportunity into a real sales
Customer + Quote. Everything else CRM (campaigns, marketing automation, contact/account hierarchies,
forecasting/pipeline analytics, service tickets, opportunity teams/competitors) is explicitly OUT of
v1 — recorded in the parity doc (D-057).

THE CROSS-MODULE CONVERT MODEL (the load-bearing idea, D-057 / D-011 / STRUCTURE §5). The
opportunity → customer + quote conversion is a SALES write (a Customer + a Quote are sales-owned
documents). CRM MUST NOT import sales/service (STRUCTURE §5). So `convert_opportunity` PUBLISHES an
``OpportunityConverted`` event and SALES' ``handlers.py`` creates the Customer (if the opportunity is
not already linked to one) AND the Quote through SALES' OWN service in the SAME transaction — exactly
the billing → AR-invoice / planned-buy → requisition precedent (the publishing module never calls the
owning module's service). CRM reads ``sales/queries`` DOWNWARD (``customer_exists`` — to skip creating
a customer when one is already linked); SALES imports ``crm/events`` declaratively (the §5 events-only
allowance, D-011). finance/inventory/sales are OLDER modules that import nothing from crm, so
crm→{sales,inventory,finance,hr}/queries is one-directional and crm←sales/events is events-only — NO
cycle (verified, D-057).

THE THREE ENTITIES (D-057).

- ``Lead`` — an unqualified inbound contact (company/contact/email/phone, source, estimated value).
  ``status`` runs NEW → CONTACTED → QUALIFIED → CONVERTED (or DISQUALIFIED). A QUALIFIED lead converts
  to an opportunity: ``convert_lead_to_opportunity`` creates the ``Opportunity``, copies the
  company/contact/value, links ``source_lead_id`` + sets the lead's ``converted_opportunity_id`` +
  status CONVERTED. Auto-numbered LEAD-… for traceability (D-057).
- ``Opportunity`` — a qualified deal in the pipeline. ``stage`` IS THE KANBAN COLUMN: PROSPECTING →
  QUALIFICATION → PROPOSAL → NEGOTIATION → WON | LOST. ``move_stage`` is the kanban move (validated
  transitions; WON/LOST are terminal). Optional ``OpportunityLine`` rows (expected products) become
  the quote lines on convert. Auto-numbered OPP-….
- ``Activity`` — a logged interaction (CALL/EMAIL/MEETING/TASK/NOTE) against EXACTLY ONE of a lead OR
  an opportunity (a service + DB CHECK enforce exactly-one-parent). ``status`` OPEN → COMPLETED |
  CANCELLED.

CROSS-MODULE IDS ARE OPAQUE (D-029/§5). ``owner_employee_id`` is an OPAQUE hr employee id (nullable,
validated via ``hr/queries.employee_exists`` when set). An opportunity's ``customer_id`` is an OPAQUE
sales customer id (nullable, validated via ``sales/queries.customer_exists`` when set). An opportunity
LINE's ``item_id`` is an OPAQUE inventory item id (validated via ``inventory/queries.item_exists``).
None of these is a cross-module FK. The ``converted_customer_id`` / ``converted_quote_id`` on a
converted opportunity are recorded for the API, but the DURABLE convert link is the docflow edge the
sales handler writes (opportunity → 'converted_to_customer'/'converted_to_quote'), not an FK — the
billing-side precedent.

Structure (each <400 lines, STRUCTURE §3/§8.4): ``constants.py``, ``models.py``, ``schemas.py``,
``service/`` (leads / opportunities / activities / convert), ``events.py``, ``queries.py``,
``router.py`` + sibling routers (ONE surface at ``/api/v1/crm``). No ``handlers.py`` here — CRM
publishes ``OpportunityConverted`` but subscribes to nothing; SALES owns the handler (D-057).
"""
